parts.text: The random variable X has the distribution N(30, σ²). Given that P(X > 36) = 0.1, find σ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The lengths of fish of a certain species caught in Keenjhar Lake are normally distributed. 15% of the fish are longer than 48 cm and 25% are shorter than 36 cm. Find the mean and standard deviation of the lengths.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The masses of watermelons sold at a market are normally distributed. The mean mass is four times the standard deviation, and 6.68% of the watermelons have a mass less than 2.5 kg. Find the mean and standard deviation.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The times taken by candidates to complete an online test are normally distributed with standard deviation 8 minutes. 20% of candidates take more than 75 minutes. Find the mean time.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the percentage of candidates who take less than 60 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Marks in an examination are normally distributed. The top 10% of candidates, who scored 78 or more, receive a distinction, and the bottom 20%, who scored 45 or less, fail. Find the mean and standard deviation of the marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the proportion of candidates scoring between 50 and 70.
parts.working:
M1 standardise both with the values from (a)
M1 Φ(0.767) − Φ(−0.520)
A1 0.477

parts.label: a
parts.text: The random variable X is normally distributed with P(X < 20) = 0.12 and P(X > 44) = 0.12. Find the mean and standard deviation of X.
parts.working:
B1 μ = 32 by symmetry
M1 z = 1.175
M1 12/σ = 1.175
A1 σ = 10.2

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X > 40).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N(20, 9) and N(15, 16) respectively. State the distribution of X + Y.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(X + Y > 40).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N(30, 5²) and N(24, 3²). Find P(X < Y).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The independent random variables X and Y have E(X) = 10, Var(X) = 4, E(Y) = 6 and Var(Y) = 2.5. Find E(3X − 2Y) and Var(3X − 2Y).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The mass of an empty glass jar is normally distributed with mean 250 g and standard deviation 8 g. The mass of honey put into a jar is normally distributed with mean 500 g and standard deviation 12 g, independently of the jar. Find the probability that a filled jar has a total mass of more than 770 g.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The masses of adults using a lift are normally distributed with mean 72 kg and standard deviation 11 kg. The lift's safe load is 600 kg. Eight adults, chosen at random, enter the lift. Find the probability that their total mass exceeds the safe load.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The random variable X has the distribution N(12, 2²). X₁, X₂, …, X₅ are five independent observations of X. Find P(X₁ + X₂ + X₃ + X₄ + X₅ > 65).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(5X > 65) and explain why this differs from your answer to (a).
parts.working:
B1 5X ~ N(60, 100)
B1 1 − Φ(0.5) = 0.309
B1 5X multiplies one observation, so variance is 25 × 4; the sum of five independent values has variance 5 × 4

parts.label: a
parts.text: Zara's journey to university has three independent stages: walking to the bus stop takes N(12, 2²) minutes, waiting for the bus takes N(8, 3²) minutes and the bus ride takes N(25, 4²) minutes. Find the probability that her total journey time is less than 40 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The lifetimes of brand A light bulbs are distributed N(1200, 150²) hours and those of brand B bulbs are distributed N(1100, 100²) hours. One bulb of each brand is chosen at random. Find the probability that the brand A bulb lasts longer than the brand B bulb.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Rods of type A have lengths distributed N(42, 1.5²) cm and rods of type B have lengths distributed N(20, 0.8²) cm. One rod of each type is chosen at random. Find the probability that the type A rod is more than twice as long as the type B rod.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The diameters of bolts are normally distributed with mean 9.8 mm and standard deviation 0.05 mm. The diameters of the holes in nuts are normally distributed with mean 10.0 mm and standard deviation 0.08 mm. A bolt fits a nut if the bolt's diameter is less than the hole's diameter. A bolt and a nut are chosen at random. Find the probability that the bolt fits the nut.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Bags of flour have masses distributed N(2.02, 0.03²) kg. Twelve bags are packed into a box whose mass is distributed N(1.5, 0.1²) kg. All masses are independent. Find the probability that the total mass of the full box is between 25.6 kg and 26.0 kg.
parts.working:
B1 mean 24.24 + 1.5 = 25.74
B1 variance 12 × 0.0009 + 0.01 = 0.0208
M1 standardise both limits: −0.971 and 1.803
M1 subtract Φ values
A1 0.798

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a 4 × 100 m relay the four runners' times, in seconds, are independent and distributed N(12.1, 0.2²), N(11.8, 0.15²), N(12.3, 0.25²) and N(11.9, 0.18²). Find the probability that the team's total time is less than 47.8 seconds.

parts.label: a
parts.text: July rainfall in Lahore is modelled as N(190, 45²) mm and July rainfall in Islamabad as N(270, 60²) mm, independently. Find the probability that in a particular July Islamabad's rainfall is more than 1.5 times Lahore's.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The midday temperature in a city in June, in °C, is distributed N(28, 4²). The temperature F in °F is given by F = 1.8C + 32. State the distribution of F.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that the midday temperature exceeds 90 °F.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A household's daily electricity use, in kWh, is distributed N(14, 3²), independently from day to day. Electricity costs Rs 55 per kWh plus a fixed charge of Rs 100 per day. Find the mean and variance of the total cost for a week (7 days).
parts.working:
B1 daily cost 55X + 100: mean 870
B1 weekly mean 7 × 870 = 6090
B1 variance 7 × 55² × 9 = 190 575

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the probability that the weekly cost exceeds Rs 6500.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Boxes have masses distributed N(15, 2²) kg independently. A trolley can safely carry 250 kg. Find the largest number of boxes, n, that can be loaded so that the probability that the total mass exceeds 250 kg is less than 0.05.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N(50, 4) and N(49, 5). Find P(|X − Y| < 3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The masses of men in a town are distributed N(78, 10²) kg and the masses of women N(62, 8²) kg. Three men and four women are chosen at random. Find the probability that the total mass of the three men is greater than the total mass of the four women.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N(μ, 3²) and N(2μ, 4²). Given that P(X + Y > 60) = 0.0228, find μ.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N(10, σ²) and N(15, 9). Given that P(2X > Y) = 0.9, find σ.
parts.working:
B1 2X − Y has mean 5
B1 variance 4σ² + 9
M1 5/√(4σ² + 9) = 1.282
M1 4σ² + 9 = 15.22
A1 σ = 1.25

parts.label: a
parts.text: A delivery driver's routes are of two types. The time for a type A route is distributed N(35, 4²) minutes and the time for a type B route is distributed N(22, 3²) minutes. On one day the driver completes 2 type A routes and 3 type B routes, all times being independent. Find the probability that the total time for the five routes is more than 140 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A machine fills bags labelled 1 kg with sugar. The mass in a bag is distributed N(1.008, 0.006²) kg. A shopkeeper buys 5 bags at random. Find the probability that the total mass of sugar in the 5 bags is less than 5 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a class, Physics marks are distributed N(58, 12²) and Chemistry marks N(62, 10²). Assuming a student's two marks are independent, find the probability that a randomly chosen student's Physics mark is at least 10 more than their Chemistry mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Comment on the independence assumption.
parts.answer: Unlikely to be true: a student good at one science is likely to do well in the other.
parts.working: B1 sensible comment that the marks are probably positively related

parts.label: a
parts.text: The random variable X has the distribution N(4, 0.5²). X₁, X₂, X₃ and X₄ are independent observations of X, and T = X₁ + X₂ + X₃ − 2X₄. Find the mean and variance of T.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find P(T < 3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A river ferry carries 20 cars and 10 vans. The masses of cars are distributed N(1.4, 0.2²) tonnes and the masses of vans N(2.6, 0.3²) tonnes, all independently. The ferry's maximum safe load is 56 tonnes. Find the probability that the total mass of the vehicles exceeds the maximum safe load.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A wall is built from 12 courses of bricks. The height of each course is distributed N(7.5, 0.2²) cm and between consecutive courses there is a layer of mortar whose thickness is distributed N(1.0, 0.15²) cm. All heights are independent. Find the probability that the height of the wall is between 100 cm and 102.5 cm.
parts.working:
B1 11 layers of mortar; mean 90 + 11 = 101
B1 variance 12 × 0.04 + 11 × 0.0225 = 0.7275
M1 z values −1.172 and 1.759
M1 subtract Φ values
A1 0.840

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a garment factory, the numbers of shirts finished in an hour by machines A, B and C are modelled by independent normal distributions N(120, 9²), N(95, 7²) and N(30, 5²). Find the probability that in a given hour machine A finishes more shirts than machines B and C together.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a normal model for these counts is only an approximation.
parts.answer: The numbers of shirts are discrete (whole numbers), while the normal distribution is continuous.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Sacks of basmati rice have masses distributed N(25.2, 0.4²) kg. A restaurant buys 4 sacks chosen at random. Find the probability that their total mass is within 0.5 kg of 100.8 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The random variable X has the distribution N(3, 1.5²) and Y = 2X + 5. State the distribution of Y and find P(Y > 15).
parts.working:
B1 mean 11
B1 variance 4 × 2.25 = 9
M1 z = 4/3
A1 0.0912

parts.label: a
parts.text: Floor tiles have lengths distributed N(30, 0.4²) cm. A row of 10 tiles is laid with a fixed gap of 0.3 cm between neighbouring tiles. The row must fit along a wall of length 303.5 cm. Find the probability that a row of 10 randomly chosen tiles, with gaps, fits.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why it would be wrong to use 10X, where X is the length of one tile, for the total length of the tiles.
parts.answer: 10X assumes all ten tiles have the same length; the tiles vary independently, so the variance is 10 × 0.16, not 100 × 0.16.
parts.working: B1 independent tiles: add variances, not multiply one tile

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (3 cos 2x − 4 sin(½x)) dx.
parts.working: B1 (3/2) sin 2x; B1 +8 cos(½x) (coefficient 8 and sign); B1 + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/3} (3 cos 2x − 4 sin(½x)) dx. Give your answer in the form a√3 + b.
parts.working: M1 substitute both limits into the result of (a); sin(2π/3) = √3/2, cos(π/6) = √3/2, cos 0 = 1; (3√3/4 + 4√3) − 8 = 19√3/4 − 8 A1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the identity sec²x ≡ 1 + tan²x to express 2 tan²x + 1 in terms of sec²x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/4} (2 tan²x + 1) dx.
parts.working: M1 integrate to 2 tan x − x; M1 apply limits; A1 2(1) − π/4 = 2 − π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express cos²3x in terms of cos 6x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₀^{π/12} cos²3x dx = π/24 + 1/12.
parts.working: M1 integrate ½ + ½cos 6x; A1 x/2 + (1/12) sin 6x; M1 limits, sin(π/2) = 1; A1 π/24 + 1/12 shown.

parts.label: a
parts.text: By expanding sin(3x + x) and sin(3x − x), show that sin 3x cos x ≡ ½(sin 4x + sin 2x).
parts.working: M1 sin(3x+x) + sin(3x−x) = 2 sin 3x cos x; A1 rearrange to the given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/6} sin 3x cos x dx.
parts.working: M1 integrate to ½(−¼ cos 4x − ½ cos 2x); A1 correct; M1 limits, cos(2π/3) = −½, cos(π/3) = ½; A1 ½[(1/8 − 1/4) − (−3/4)] = ½ × 5/8 = 5/16.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that 1/(1 + cos 2x) ≡ ½ sec²x.
parts.working: M1 use 1 + cos 2x = 2cos²x; A1 1/(2cos²x) = ½ sec²x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫_{π/6}^{π/3} (1 + 2/(1 + cos 2x)) dx, giving your answer in the form aπ + b√3.
parts.working: M1 integrand = 1 + sec²x; A1 x + tan x; M1 limits: (π/3 + √3) − (π/6 + 1/√3); A1 π/6 + 2√3/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has gradient function dy/dx = 6x² − 4x + 1 and passes through the point (2, 9). Find the equation of the curve.
parts.working: M1 integrate (power of each term increased by 1); A1 2x³ − 2x² + x + c; M1 substitute (2, 9): 16 − 8 + 2 + c = 9; A1 c = −1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve passes through the point (4, 5) and its gradient is given by dy/dx = 3/√(2x + 1). Find the equation of the curve.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinate of the point where the curve crosses the x-axis.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point (4, 5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has d²y/dx² = 12x − 6. The curve has a stationary point at (1, 2). Find dy/dx and hence find the equation of the curve.
parts.working: M1 integrate: dy/dx = 6x² − 6x + c; A1 dy/dx = 0 at x = 1 gives c = 0; M1 integrate again: y = 2x³ − 3x² + k; M1 substitute (1, 2); A1 k = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coordinates of the other stationary point and determine the nature of each stationary point.
parts.answer: (0, 3) is a maximum; (1, 2) is a minimum
parts.working: B1 6x² − 6x = 0 gives x = 0, y = 3; M1 d²y/dx² at x = 0 is −6 < 0, maximum; A1 at x = 1, d²y/dx² = 6 > 0, minimum.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x e^{2x} dx.
parts.working: M1 parts with u = x, dv/dx = e^{2x}; A1 ½x e^{2x} − ¼e^{2x}; M1 apply limits; A1 (½e² − ¼e²) − (−¼) = ¼(e² + 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₁^e x² ln x dx = (2e³ + 1)/9.
parts.working: M1 parts with u = ln x, dv/dx = x²; A1 (x³/3) ln x − ∫ x²/3 dx; A1 (x³/3) ln x − x³/9; M1 limits, ln e = 1, ln 1 = 0; A1 e³/3 − e³/9 + 1/9 = (2e³ + 1)/9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use integration by parts twice to find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/2} x² cos x dx.
parts.working: M1 first parts: x² sin x − ∫ 2x sin x dx; A1; M1 second parts: ∫ 2x sin x dx = −2x cos x + 2 sin x; A1 x² sin x + 2x cos x − 2 sin x; M1 limits; A1 π²/4 − 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 2x − 1 to find the exact value of ∫₁⁵ x/√(2x − 1) dx.
parts.working: B1 x = (u+1)/2, dx = ½ du, limits u = 1 to 9; M1 integrand becomes ¼(u^{½} + u^{−½}); A1 ¼[(2/3)u^{3/2} + 2u^{½}]; M1 limits; A1 ¼(24 − 8/3) = 16/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 1 + x² to show that ∫₀^{√3} x³/√(1 + x²) dx = 4/3.
parts.working: B1 du = 2x dx and x² = u − 1; B1 limits 1 and 4; M1 integrand ½(u − 1)u^{−½} = ½(u^{½} − u^{−½}); A1 ½[(2/3)u^{3/2} − 2u^{½}]; M1 limits; A1 ½(4/3 + 4/3) = 4/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution x = 2 sin θ to find the exact value of ∫₀¹ 1/(4 − x²)^{3/2} dx.
parts.working: B1 dx = 2cos θ dθ; M1 (4 − 4sin²θ)^{3/2} = 8cos³θ; A1 integrand ¼ sec²θ; B1 limits 0 and π/6; M1 integrate to ¼ tan θ; A1 ¼ × 1/√3 = √3/12.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where the line y = x + 3 meets the curve y = x² − 2x + 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the line and the curve.
parts.working: M1 ∫₀³ ((x + 3) − (x² − 2x + 3)) dx; A1 integrand 3x − x²; M1 [3x²/2 − x³/3]₀³; A1 27/2 − 9 = 9/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 4√x and the line y = x meet at the origin O and at the point A. Find the coordinates of A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 4 − x² passes through P(1, 3). Find the equation of the normal to the curve at P.
parts.working: B1 dy/dx = −2x = −2 at P; M1 normal gradient ½; A1 y − 3 = ½(x − 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The normal meets the curve again at Q. Find the x-coordinate of Q.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve and the normal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (2x + 5)/(x + 1) can be written as 2 + 3/(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀² (2x + 5)/(x + 1) dx.
parts.working: M1 integrate to 2x + 3 ln(x + 1); A1; A1 (4 + 3 ln 3) − 0 = 4 + 3 ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ (4x + 2)/(x² + x + 1) dx, giving your answer as a single logarithm.
parts.working: M1 recognise 4x + 2 = 2 × d/dx(x² + x + 1); A1 2 ln(x² + x + 1); A1 2 ln 3 − 2 ln 1 = ln 9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (e^{2x} + 3e^{−x}) dx.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₀^{ln 2} (e^{2x} + 3e^{−x}) dx = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k 4e^{2x} dx = 10, find the exact value of k.
parts.working: M1 integrate to 2e^{2x}; M1 2e^{2k} − 2 = 10; A1 e^{2k} = 6, k = ½ ln 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ (eˣ + 1)² dx.
parts.working: M1 expand e^{2x} + 2eˣ + 1; A1 ½e^{2x} + 2eˣ + x; M1 limits; A1 (½e² + 2e + 1) − (½ + 2) = ½e² + 2e − 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁⁴ (3√x − 2/x²) dx.
parts.working: M1 increase powers: 2x^{3/2} + 2x^{−1}; A1 each term correct (A1 A1 if separate); M1 limits (16 + ½) − (2 + 2); A1 12.5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 4/(2x + 1)³ dx.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the value of the improper integral ∫₁^∞ 4/(2x + 1)³ dx, explaining how the upper limit is dealt with.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the curve y = √(x + 1), the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 3 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀³ (x + 1) dx; A1 π[x²/2 + x]; M1 limits; A1 π(9/2 + 3) = 15π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = 5 meets the curve y = x² + 1 at the points A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The region enclosed between the curve and the line is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫_{−2}^{2} (5² − (x² + 1)²) dx; M1 expand (x² + 1)² = x⁴ + 2x² + 1; A1 integrand 24 − 2x² − x⁴; A1 [24x − 2x³/3 − x⁵/5]; M1 limits (or 2 × from 0 to 2); A1 2π(48 − 16/3 − 32/5) = 1088π/15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x³ − 6x² + 8x crosses the x-axis at O, A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area of the regions enclosed between the curve and the x-axis from x = 0 to x = 4.
parts.working: M1 integrate to x⁴/4 − 2x³ + 4x²; A1 ∫₀² = 4; A1 ∫₂⁴ = −4 (region below the axis); A1 total area 4 + 4 = 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the curve y = 9/(x + 1)², the x-axis and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: M1 integrate to −9/(x + 1); M1 limits −3 − (−9); A1 6.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line x = k divides this region into two parts of equal area. Find k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 5/((x − 1)(x + 4)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₂⁴ 5/((x − 1)(x + 4)) dx, giving your answer as a single logarithm.
parts.working: M1 ln(x − 1) − ln(x + 4); M1 limits (ln 3 − ln 8) − (ln 1 − ln 6); A1 ln(18/8) = ln(9/4).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x² + 3)/(x²(x + 1)) in partial fractions.
parts.working: B1 form A/x + B/x² + C/(x + 1); M1 2x² + 3 = Ax(x + 1) + B(x + 1) + Cx²; A1 B = 3, C = 5; A1 A = −3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₁² (2x² + 3)/(x²(x + 1)) dx = 3/2 + 5 ln 3 − 8 ln 2.
parts.working: M1 integrate: −3 ln x − 3/x + 5 ln(x + 1); A1 (follow through); M1 limits: (−3 ln 2 − 3/2 + 5 ln 3) − (−3 + 5 ln 2); A1 3/2 + 5 ln 3 − 8 ln 2; A1 fully correct log work.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (2x + 3)/(x² + 1) dx.
parts.working: M1 split into 2x/(x² + 1) + 3/(x² + 1); A1 ln(x² + 1); A1 3 tan⁻¹x + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀¹ (2x + 3)/(x² + 1) dx.
parts.working: M1 limits, tan⁻¹1 = π/4; A1 ln 2 + 3π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Kxⁿ, where K and n are constants. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line passing through the points (0.5, 2.1) and (2.5, 0.9). Find the values of n and K, giving K correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = A × bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line through (1, 3.2) and (4, 5.0). Find the values of A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 ln y = ln A + x ln b; M1 gradient 1.8/3 = 0.6 = ln b; M1 intercept ln A = 3.2 − 0.6 = 2.6; A1 A = 13.5, b = 1.82.

stem:
A laboratory culture of bacteria is counted every 2 hours. The number N of bacteria after t hours is modelled by N = N₀e^{kt}.
t (hours): 0, 2, 4, 6, 8
N: 250, 503, 1014, 2042, 4111

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the model N = N₀e^{kt} gives a straight line when ln N is plotted against t, and state what the gradient and intercept represent.
parts.answer: ln N = ln N₀ + kt; gradient k, intercept ln N₀
parts.working: M1 take ln of both sides; A1 gradient k, vertical intercept ln N₀.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the values of ln N for the table, correct to 2 decimal places, and use them to estimate k and N₀.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Use the model to estimate the number of bacteria after 10 hours, correct to 2 significant figures, and comment on the reliability of this estimate.
parts.answer: About 8300; it is an extrapolation beyond the data, so less reliable

author: HomiLabs

stem: A student in Lahore times a simple pendulum. The period T seconds and the length L metres are thought to satisfy T = kLⁿ. The graph of ln T against ln L is a straight line passing through the points (−1.20, 0.096) and (0.40, 0.896).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of n and k, giving k correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use your values to find the period of a pendulum of length 0.75 m, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy the equation y² = A bˣ, where A and b are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line passing through (2, 1.45) and (5, 0.70). Find the values of A and b correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 2 ln y = ln A + x ln b, so ln y = ½ ln A + (½ ln b)x; M1 gradient −0.75/3 = −0.25 = ½ ln b; A1 b = e^{−0.5} = 0.607; M1 intercept 1.45 + 0.5 = 1.95 = ½ ln A; A1 A = e^{3.9} = 49.4.

stem: A cup of tea cools in a room at 20 °C. Its temperature θ °C after t minutes is modelled by θ − 20 = Ae^{−kt}. Readings: t = 0, θ = 80.0; t = 5, θ = 60.2; t = 10, θ = 47.0; t = 15, θ = 38.07.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the model gives a straight line when ln(θ − 20) is plotted against t, stating the gradient and intercept in terms of A and k.
parts.answer: ln(θ − 20) = ln A − kt; gradient −k, intercept ln A

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the readings at t = 0 and t = 15 to find the values of A and k, correct to 2 significant figures where necessary.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the tea to cool to 30 °C, correct to 3 significant figures.

stem: The population P million of a large city is modelled by P = a × bᵗ, where t is the number of years after the start of 2010. The graph of ln P against t is a straight line through (2, 2.65) and (10, 2.97).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the values of a and b, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the model to find the value of t when the population first reaches 25 million, and state the calendar year in which this happens.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Axⁿ. When x = 2, y = 15 and when x = 5, y = 60. By taking natural logarithms, find the values of n and A correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln 15 = ln A + n ln 2 and ln 60 = ln A + n ln 5; M1 subtract: ln 4 = n ln 2.5; A1 n = 1.51; M1 substitute back; A1 A = 15 ÷ 2^{1.513} = 5.26.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence state the gradient and the intercept on the vertical axis of the graph of ln y against ln x.
parts.working: B1 gradient n = 1.51; B1 intercept ln A = 1.66.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y = Ae^{−kx²}. Explain why the graph of ln y against x² is a straight line.
parts.answer: ln y = ln A − kx², which is linear in x²

parts.label: b
parts.text: This line passes through (1.0, 2.20) and (4.0, 1.30), where the horizontal axis shows x². Find A and k.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find y when x = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: For the relationship y = A bˣ, state which graph should be drawn to give a straight line, and what its gradient represents.
parts.answer: ln y against x; gradient ln b
parts.working: B1 ln y against x; B1 gradient = ln b (intercept ln A).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The line obtained has equation ln y = 0.92 + 0.35x. Find A and b, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 3^{2x} = 20, giving x correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation log₂(x + 5) − log₂(x − 1) = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 2 ln x − ln(x + 6) = ln 2. Give your answer in exact form and correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln(x²/(x + 6)) = ln 2; A1 x² − 2x − 12 = 0; M1 solve: x = 1 ± √13; A1 x = 1 + √13 (4.61) only, since ln x needs x > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation e^{2x} − 5eˣ + 6 = 0, giving your answers in exact form.
parts.working: M1 let u = eˣ: u² − 5u + 6 = 0; A1 u = 2, 3; A1 x = ln 2, ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 5^{x+1} = 3^{2x−1}. Show that x = ln 15 / ln(9/5) and give x correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 (x + 1) ln 5 = (2x − 1) ln 3; M1 collect x terms: x(2 ln 3 − ln 5) = ln 5 + ln 3; A1 x = ln 15/ln(9/5); A1 4.61.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation 2^{2x+1} − 7(2ˣ) + 3 = 0, giving any non-integer answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: B1 2^{2x+1} = 2(2ˣ)²; M1 2u² − 7u + 3 = 0; A1 u = 3 or ½; M1 2ˣ = 3 gives x = ln 3/ln 2; A1 x = 1.58 and x = −1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation ln(3x − 2) = 2, giving x in exact form and correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that log₉ x = ½ log₃ x.
parts.working: M1 change of base log₉ x = log₃ x / log₃ 9; A1 log₃ 9 = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve log₃ x + log₉ x = 6.
parts.working: M1 (3/2) log₃ x = 6; A1 log₃ x = 4, x = 81.

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 5 kg rests in equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the normal reaction and the frictional force acting on the box.
parts.answer: R = 45.3 N, F = 21.1 N up the slope
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular: R = 50 cos 25°; A1 45.3 N; B1 F = 50 sin 25° = 21.1 N.

parts.label: b

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 8 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 20° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. A force of magnitude P N acts on the crate up the line of greatest slope.

parts.text: Find the least value of P for which the crate remains at rest.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of P for which the crate remains at rest.
parts.working: M1 friction now down the slope: P = 80 sin 20° + 22.55; A1 49.9 N.

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 4 kg rests on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal, with coefficient of friction 0.2. A horizontal force of magnitude P N, in the vertical plane containing the line of greatest slope, acts on the block towards the plane, and the block is about to move up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the normal reaction is (40 cos 30° + P sin 30°) N.
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular to the plane, horizontal force has component P sin 30° into the plane; A1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of P.
parts.working: M1 resolve along the plane: P cos 30° = 40 sin 30° + F; M1 F = 0.2R; A1 P(cos 30° − 0.2 sin 30°) = 20 + 8 cos 30°; A1 P = 35.2.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A box of mass 6 kg is on a rough ramp inclined at 10° to the horizontal at a warehouse in Faisalabad. A rope pulls the box with a force of 30 N acting at 15° above the line of greatest slope, up the ramp. The box is about to move up the ramp.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the box and the ramp.
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular: R + 30 sin 15° = 60 cos 10°; A1 R = 51.32 N; M1 resolve parallel: 30 cos 15° = F + 60 sin 10°; A1 F = 18.56 N; M1 μ = F/R; A1 0.362.

author: HomiLabs

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 2.5 kg is on a rough plane inclined at 35° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.4. A force of magnitude P N acts on the particle at an angle of 20° above the line of greatest slope, directed up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the set of values of P for which the particle remains in equilibrium.
parts.working: M1 resolve perpendicular: R = 25 cos 35° − P sin 20°; M1 about to slide up: P cos 20° = 25 sin 35° + 0.4R; A1 P = 20.9; M1 about to slide down: P cos 20° + 0.4R = 25 sin 35°; A1 P = 7.66; M1 both cases used with correct friction directions; A1 7.66 ≤ P ≤ 20.9; B1 check R > 0 in both cases.

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the greatest angle of a slope on which a block can rest without any applied force, if the coefficient of friction is 0.5.

parts.text: A block of mass 3 kg is placed on a slope inclined at 40° with the same coefficient of friction, and a force of 12 N acts on it up the line of greatest slope. Determine whether the block remains at rest, and find the magnitude and direction of the frictional force.
parts.answer: Remains at rest; friction 7.28 N up the slope

stem: Three forces act at a point O: 6 N along the positive x-axis, 8 N along the positive y-axis, and F N acting in the third quadrant at an angle θ below the negative x-axis. The resultant of the three forces is 5 N along the positive y-axis.

parts.label: a

stem: Three horizontal ropes pull on a ring fixed to a post on a boat at Keamari harbour. The forces are 25 N on a bearing of 040°, 18 N on a bearing of 160° and 30 N on a bearing of 270°.

parts.label: a

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A lantern of mass 2 kg hangs in equilibrium from two light strings. One string makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal and the other makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal, on the other side.

parts.label: a

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Two points A and B are on a horizontal ceiling, 1.0 m apart. A particle C of mass 5 kg is attached to light inextensible strings AC and BC, of lengths 0.8 m and 0.6 m, and hangs in equilibrium below AB.

parts.label: a

stem: A particle of weight 20 N hangs in equilibrium from two light strings. One string has tension 15 N and makes an angle of 25° above the horizontal. The other string, on the opposite side, has tension T N and makes an angle θ above the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find T and θ.
parts.working: M1 horizontal: T cos θ = 15 cos 25°; M1 vertical: T sin θ + 15 sin 25° = 20; A1 T cos θ = 13.59, T sin θ = 13.66; A1 T = 19.3; A1 θ = 45.1°.

author: HomiLabs

stem: A light inextensible string of length 1.8 m has its ends fixed at points A and B on the same horizontal level, 1.2 m apart. A small smooth ring of weight 6 N is threaded on the string.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The ring hangs at rest at the midpoint of the string. Find the tension in the string, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 each half 0.9 m with horizontal 0.6 m, so vertical drop √(0.9² − 0.6²) = √0.45 = 0.671 m and sine of angle to horizontal = 0.671/0.9 = 0.745; M1 2T × 0.745 = 6; A1 T = 4.02 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A horizontal force of magnitude F N, acting in the direction from A to B, is now applied to the ring, so that it rests vertically below B with both parts of the string taut. Show that the ring is 0.5 m below B, and find the tension in the string and the value of F.
parts.working: M1 AR = 1.8 − BR and AR² = 1.2² + BR², so (1.8 − d)² = 1.44 + d²; A1 d = 0.5, AR = 1.3; B1 tension the same in both parts (smooth ring); M1 vertical: T + T × (5/13) = 6, so T = 13/3 = 4.33 N; A1 horizontal: F = T × 12/13 = 4 N.

check: abs(2.7/math.sqrt(0.45)-4.02)<0.005 and abs((1.8-0.5)**2-(1.44+0.5**2))<1e-9 and Fraction(6)/(1+Fraction(5,13))==Fraction(13,3) and Fraction(13,3)*Fraction(12,13)==4

author: HomiLabs

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A sack of rice of mass 20 kg lies on a rough horizontal floor in a godown. The coefficient of friction is 0.5. A force of magnitude P N is applied at an angle θ above the horizontal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the sack is about to move when P = 100/(cos θ + 0.5 sin θ).
parts.working: M1 R = 200 − P sin θ; M1 P cos θ = 0.5R; A1 rearrange to the given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of P when θ = 30°, and the corresponding normal reaction.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Compare your answer to part (b) with the force needed when the sack is pulled horizontally, and explain the difference.
parts.answer: Horizontal pull needs P = 100 N, more than 89.6 N; pulling upwards reduces the normal reaction and hence the maximum friction
parts.working: B1 θ = 0 gives P = 100 N > 89.6 N; B1 the upward component reduces R, so limiting friction 0.5R is smaller.

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block P of mass 2 kg is on a rough horizontal table, with coefficient of friction 0.4. stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particles A and B, of masses 3 kg and m kg (m > 3), are connected by a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth pulley and released from rest. After 1.5 s the particles are moving with speed 3 m s⁻¹. At this instant the string breaks. Neither particle hits the pulley or the ground in the motion described.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the particles before the string breaks, and hence find m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time from the instant the string breaks until A returns to its starting position.
parts.working: A rose ½ × 2 × 1.5² = 2.25 m (B1). After the break, taking up as positive: −2.25 = 3t − 5t² (M1). 5t² − 3t − 2.25 = 0 (A1). t = (3 + √54)/10 = 1.03 s (A1).

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Blocks A and B, of masses 3 kg and 2 kg, are on a rough plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. They are connected by a light inextensible string parallel to a line of greatest slope, with B below A. A force of 50 N, acting up the plane parallel to a line of greatest slope, is applied to A. The coefficient of friction between each block and the plane is 0.2.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the tension in the string is 20 N.
parts.working: B: T − 20 sin 30° − 3.464 = 2a (M1). T = 10 + 3.464 + 2 × 3.2679 = 20 N (A1). (Because both blocks have the same μ and slope, T = 50 × 2/5 exactly.)

stem: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A fixed wedge has two faces: face 1 is smooth and inclined at 30° to the horizontal, and face 2 is rough and inclined at 60° to the horizontal. The system is released from rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that B moves down face 2.
parts.answer: Weight component of B down face 2 = 25.98 N > 20 N + friction 3 N
parts.working: B: 30 sin 60° = 25.98 N; A: 40 sin 30° = 20 N (M1). Even with maximum friction 0.2 × 30 cos 60° = 3 N opposing, 25.98 > 23, so B moves down (A1).

parts.working: Friction acts down the plane: a = g sin 25° + 0.3g cos 25° (M1 A1) = 6.95 m s⁻² (A1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance it travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.

parts.answer: tan 25° = 0.466 > 0.3, so it slides; speed 3.73 m s⁻¹
parts.working: tan 25° > μ, so the weight component exceeds limiting friction (B1). Down: a = 10(sin 25° − 0.3 cos 25°) = 1.5073 (M1 A1). v = √(2 × 1.5073 × 4.6076) = 3.73 m s⁻¹ (A1).

parts.working: Arrange the other 5 people: 5! = 120 (B1). Choose the pair and its order: 3 × 2 = 6 (M1). Place the pair-unit and the third person in different gaps among the 6 gaps: 6 × 5 = 30 (M1). 120 × 6 × 30 = 21 600 (A1).

stem: Six men and four women, all different, sit in a row of ten seats at a wedding in Faisalabad.

parts.text: A car windscreen wiper arm is pivoted at a point O. The rubber blade lies along the arm from 15 cm to 50 cm from O. In one sweep the arm turns through an angle of 2.1 radians. Find the area of windscreen cleaned in one sweep. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Area = ½ × 50² × 2.1 − ½ × 15² × 2.1 M1 M1 (difference of two sectors); = 2388.75 ≈ 2390 cm² A1

parts.text: The minute hand of the clock on a clock tower in Faisalabad is 1.8 m long. Find the angle, in radians, that the minute hand turns through in 20 minutes.

parts.text: Points A and B lie on a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm, and angle AOB = 1.2 radians. Find the length of the chord AB.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: Points A and B lie on a circle with centre O and radius 8 cm. The chord AB has length 10 cm. Show that angle AOB = 1.350 radians, correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.working: sin(½AOB) = 5/8 M1; AOB = 2 sin⁻¹(0.625) = 1.3503 A1 (or cosine rule: cos AOB = (64 + 64 − 100)/128)

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: The sector OAB has centre O, radius 5 cm and angle AOB = 0.9 radians. The tangent to the arc at A meets the line OB extended at T. Find the area of the region bounded by AT, TB and the arc AB, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: A badge is made from an equilateral triangle ABC of side 4 cm. Each side is replaced by an arc of a circle centred at the opposite vertex (for example, arc BC has centre A and radius 4 cm). Find, in terms of π, the perimeter of the badge.
parts.working: Each arc = 4 × π/3 M1; total = 3 × 4π/3 = 4π A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the area of the badge is 8(π − √3) cm².
parts.working: Triangle area = ½ × 16 × sin(π/3) = 4√3 B1; each segment = ½ × 16 × π/3 − 4√3 = 8π/3 − 4√3 M1 A1; total = 4√3 + 3(8π/3 − 4√3) = 8π − 8√3 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A chord AB of a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm subtends an angle of 2π/3 radians at O. Find the exact area of the minor segment cut off by AB.
parts.working: Sector = ½ × 36 × 2π/3 = 12π B1; triangle = ½ × 36 × sin(2π/3) = 9√3 B1; segment = 12π − 9√3 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact perimeter of the minor segment.
parts.working: Arc = 6 × 2π/3 = 4π B1; AB = 2 × 6 sin(π/3) = 6√3 M1; perimeter = 4π + 6√3 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: OABC is a rhombus with sides of length 7 cm and angle AOC = 1.1 radians. An arc AC of a circle with centre O and radius 7 cm is drawn inside the rhombus. Find the area of the region inside the rhombus but outside the sector OAC, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the perimeter of this region.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sector of a circle has radius r cm and angle θ radians. The perimeter of the sector is equal to twice the length of its arc. Find θ.

parts.label: b

parts.working: ½r² × 2 = 36 M1; r = 6 A1; perimeter = 12 + 12 = 24 cm A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circular garden in the middle of a roundabout in Lahore has centre O and radius 15 m. A straight footpath crosses the garden along a chord AB of length 24 m. Find angle AOB in radians, correct to 4 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the smaller of the two parts into which the path divides the garden, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The sector OAB has centre O, radius 9 cm and angle AOB = 1.2 radians. The point C lies on OA with OC = 5 cm. Find the area of the region R bounded by the line segments CA and CB and the arc AB, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Sector = ½ × 81 × 1.2 = 48.6 B1; triangle OCB = ½ × 5 × 9 × sin 1.2 = 20.97 M1; R = 27.6 cm² A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the perimeter of R, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Two circles intersect at A and B. The first has centre P and radius 6 cm; the second has centre Q and radius 8 cm, and PQ = 10 cm. Show that angle PAQ is a right angle, and find angles APB and AQB in radians, correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.working: 6² + 8² = 10² so PAQ = 90° (converse of Pythagoras) B1; cos APQ = 6/10 M1; APB = 2 cos⁻¹ 0.6 = 1.855 A1; AQB = 2 cos⁻¹ 0.8 = 1.287 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region common to both circles, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Segment in circle P: ½ × 36(1.8546 − sin 1.8546) = 16.10 M1 A1; segment in circle Q: ½ × 64(1.2870 − sin 1.2870) = 10.46 M1; total = 26.6 cm² A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A farmer in Sindh uses 24 m of fencing to enclose a sector-shaped pen of radius r m and angle θ radians. The fencing goes along both radii and the arc. Show that the area A m² of the pen is given by A = 12r − r².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the maximum area of the pen and the value of θ for which it occurs.
parts.answer: Maximum area 36 m² when r = 6 and θ = 2
parts.working: dA/dr = 12 − 2r = 0 (or complete the square: 36 − (r − 6)²) M1; r = 6, A = 36 A1; θ = (24 − 12)/6 = 2 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Three pipes, each with a circular cross-section of radius 5 cm, are tied together so that each pipe touches the other two. Find the exact area of the cross-section of the gap enclosed between the three pipes.
parts.working: Centres form an equilateral triangle of side 10 B1; triangle area = ½ × 100 × sin(π/3) = 25√3 M1; three sectors of angle π/3: 3 × ½ × 25 × π/3 = 25π/2 M1; gap = 25√3 − 25π/2 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence give this area correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sector OAB has centre O, radius 12 cm and angle AOB = π/3. A circle with centre C and radius r cm lies inside the sector and touches OA, OB and the arc AB. Show that OC = 2r and hence find r.
parts.working: C lies on the bisector of angle AOB, so the angle between OC and OA is π/6 B1; r = OC sin(π/6) so OC = 2r M1 A1; OC + r = 12 ⇒ 3r = 12, r = 4 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find, in terms of π, the area of the part of the sector that lies outside the circle.
parts.working: Sector = ½ × 144 × π/3 = 24π; circle = 16π M1; 24π − 16π = 8π A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Triangle ABC is isosceles with AB = AC = 10 cm and angle BAC = 0.8 radians. An arc BC is drawn with centre A and radius 10 cm. A semicircle is drawn on BC as diameter, on the side of BC away from A. Find the length of BC, correct to 4 significant figures.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region inside the semicircle but outside the sector ABC, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: Semicircle = ½π(3.894)² = 23.82 M1 A1; segment of sector = ½ × 100(0.8 − sin 0.8) = 4.132 M1 A1; region = 23.82 − 4.13 = 19.7 cm² A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: ABCD is a square of side 8 cm. Two quarter circles of radius 8 cm are drawn inside the square, one with centre A passing through B and D, and one with centre C passing through B and D. Find, in terms of π, the perimeter of the leaf-shaped region that lies inside both quarter circles.
parts.working: Each arc = 8 × π/2 = 4π M1; perimeter = 8π A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the area of the leaf-shaped region is 32(π − 2) cm².
parts.working: Half the leaf = quarter circle − triangle ABD = 16π − 32 M1 A1; leaf = 2(16π − 32) = 32π − 64 = 32(π − 2) A1

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the percentage of the square that lies outside the leaf, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a rice mill, a tight belt passes around two pulleys with radii 9 cm and 4 cm. The centres of the pulleys are 13 cm apart. The straight parts of the belt are common external tangents to the two circles. Show that each straight part has length 12 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Let α = sin⁻¹(5/13). Explain why the belt is in contact with the larger pulley over an angle of (π + 2α) radians, and find α correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.working: Radii to the tangent points are perpendicular to the straight parts, which make angle α with the line of centres where sin α = 5/13 M1; so the contact angle on the larger pulley is π + 2α (and on the smaller π − 2α) A1; α = 0.3948 B1

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the total length of the belt, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A street vendor in Karachi makes paper cones for roasted chana. Each cone is made by joining the two straight edges of a sector of paper of radius 15 cm and angle θ radians, without overlap. The circular rim of the cone has radius 6 cm. Find θ, giving your answer as an exact multiple of π.
parts.working: Arc length = circumference of rim: 15θ = 2π × 6 M1; θ = 12π/15 = 4π/5 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find, in terms of π, the area of paper used for each cone.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the volume of chana a full cone can hold, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A circle has centre O and radius 5 cm. A point T is 13 cm from O, and the tangents from T touch the circle at A and B. Show that angle AOB = 2.352 radians, correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.working: OA ⟂ TA, so cos AOT = 5/13 M1; AOB = 2 cos⁻¹(5/13) = 2.3520 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by TA, TB and the minor arc AB, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the perimeter of this region, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A window in a Mughal-style building is a rectangle 1.2 m wide and 1.5 m tall, topped by a pointed arch. The arch is formed by two arcs, each of radius 1.2 m. One arc has its centre at the top left corner of the rectangle and the other at the top right corner; the arcs meet at the top point P of the window. Explain why the centres of the arcs and P form an equilateral triangle, and show that the area of the arch region above the rectangle is (0.48π − 0.36√3) m².
parts.working: Each centre is 1.2 m from P and the centres are 1.2 m apart, so all sides are 1.2 m B1; each arc subtends π/3 at its centre B1; arch = 2 × ½ × 1.44 × π/3 − ½ × 1.44 × sin(π/3) M1; = 0.48π − 0.36√3 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area of the window, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the perimeter of the window, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) is defined by p(x) = 2x³ + ax² − 13x + 6, where a is a constant. It is given that (x − 2) is a factor of p(x). Find the value of a.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence factorise p(x) completely and solve the equation p(x) = 0.
parts.working: Divide by (x − 2) to get 2x² + 5x − 3 M1 A1; = (2x − 1)(x + 3) A1; x = 2, 1/2, −3 A1

parts.text: Find the remainder when x⁴ − 3x³ + 2x − 5 is divided by (x + 2).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the remainder when x⁴ − 3x³ + 2x − 5 is divided by (2x − 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial x³ + ax² + bx − 8 has a factor (x + 1), and leaves a remainder of −12 when divided by (x − 2). Find the values of a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Factorise the polynomial and hence find the exact roots of the equation x³ + ax² + bx − 8 = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = 6x³ + ax² + bx + 2, where a and b are constants, has a factor (2x + 1) and leaves remainder −6 when divided by (x − 1). Find a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence solve the equation 6e³ʸ − 11e²ʸ − 3eʸ + 2 = 0, giving your answers correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = x³ − 4x² + ax + b has a factor (x − 3). When p(x) is divided by (x − 2) the remainder is the same as when p(x) is divided by (x + 2). Find a and b.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the remainder when p(x) is divided by (x − 2).

parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = 4x³ + ax² + bx − 3 has factors (2x − 1) and (x + 1). Find the values of a and b.

parts.text: Hence find the third factor of p(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Solve the equation 4cos³θ + 8cos²θ + cos θ − 3 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.
parts.working: cos θ = ½, −1, −3/2 M1; −3/2 has no solutions A1; θ = 60°, 300°, 180° A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx + c leaves remainders 2, 5 and 14 when divided by (x − 1), (x − 2) and (x − 3) respectively. Find a, b and c.
parts.working: Three equations: a + b + c = 1, 4a + 2b + c = −3, 9a + 3b + c = −13 M1 A1; eliminate c: 3a + b = −4, 5a + b = −10 M1; a = −3, b = 5 A1; c = −1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the equation p(x) = 0 has exactly one real root, and state two consecutive integers between which it lies.
parts.answer: Exactly one real root, between 0 and 1
parts.working: p′(x) = 3x² − 6x + 5, discriminant 36 − 60 < 0 so p′(x) > 0 for all x and p is increasing M1 A1; p(0) = −1 < 0, p(1) = 2 > 0, so root between 0 and 1 B1

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (x − 3) is a factor of p(x) = 2x³ + ax² − 11x + 6, find a and factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve the equation 2|x|³ − 3x² − 11|x| + 6 = 0.
parts.working: x² = |x|², so this is p(|x|) = 0 with |x| = 3 or ½ (|x| = −2 rejected) M1; x = ±3, ±½ A1

parts.label: c
parts.text: Hence solve the equation 2(27ʸ) − 3(9ʸ) − 11(3ʸ) + 6 = 0, giving any non-exact answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: 3ʸ = 3, ½ (−2 rejected) M1; y = 1 A1; y = ln ½ / ln 3 = −0.631 A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + kx² − 4x − 4k, where k is a constant. Show that (x + k) is a factor of p(x) for all values of k.
parts.working: p(−k) = −k³ + k³ + 4k − 4k M1; = 0, so (x + k) is a factor A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: When p(x) is divided by (x − 3) the remainder is 30. Find k and factorise p(x) completely.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the values of k for which the equation p(x) = 0 has exactly two distinct real roots.
parts.working: p(x) = (x + k)(x − 2)(x + 2), so there is a repeated root when −k = 2 or −k = −2 M1; k = ±2 A1

parts.text: Sketch, on the same axes, the graphs of y = |x − 2| and y = 3x − 4, labelling where each meets the axes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the equation |x − 3| = 2|x + 1|.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence solve the equation |eʸ − 3| = 2|eʸ + 1|, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.text: The constant a is positive. Solve the inequality |2x − a| > |x + a|, giving your answer in terms of a.
parts.working: Square: 4x² − 4ax + a² > x² + 2ax + a² M1; 3x² − 6ax > 0 A1; 3x(x − 2a) > 0, critical values 0 and 2a A1; x < 0 or x > 2a A1

parts.text: Hence solve the inequality |2 ln t − 3| > |ln t + 3|, giving the boundary value correct to 4 significant figures where appropriate.

parts.text: Let f(x) = (4x² + 3x + 14)/((x + 2)(x² + 4)). Express f(x) in partial fractions.

parts.text: Hence show that the integral of f(x) from x = 0 to x = 2 is equal to (7/2) ln 2 + π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + 7)/((x − 1)(x + 3)) in the form A + B/(x − 1) + C/(x + 3), where A, B and C are constants.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The polynomial x⁴ + 2x³ + ax + b, where a and b are constants, is divided by x² + x − 2. The remainder is 3x + 1. Find the quotient and the values of a and b.
parts.working: Divide: quotient x² + x + 1 M1 A1; remainder (a + 1)x + (b + 2) A1; a + 1 = 3, a = 2 A1; b + 2 = 1, b = −1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Using these values of a and b, find the remainder when the polynomial is divided by (x − 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the quotient and remainder when 2x³ + x² + 4x + 5 is divided by x² + 1.
parts.working: Long division M1; quotient 2x + 1 A1; remainder 2x + 4 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of the integral of (2x³ + x² + 4x + 5)/(x² + 1) with respect to x from 0 to 1.
parts.working: Integrand = 2x + 1 + 2x/(x² + 1) + 4/(x² + 1) B1; [x² + x] B1; ln(x² + 1) B1; 4 tan⁻¹x B1; = 2 + ln 2 + π A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line. Its velocity t seconds after leaving a fixed point O is v m s⁻¹, where v = 6t − t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6. Find the acceleration of the particle when t = 2.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at a point O and moves in a straight line. Its acceleration t seconds later is (4 − 2t) m s⁻². Find an expression for the velocity of the particle in terms of t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the displacement of the particle from O when it next comes to instantaneous rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at O and moves in a straight line. For 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 its velocity is v = 1.5t² − 0.25t³ m s⁻¹. For t ≥ 4 it decelerates uniformly, its velocity being v = 24 − 4t, until it comes to rest. Find the maximum acceleration of the particle for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the velocity is continuous at t = 4 and find the time at which the particle comes to rest.
parts.answer: v(4) = 8 in both; rest at t = 6

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by the particle.
parts.working: ∫₀⁴(1.5t² − 0.25t³) dt = [0.5t³ − t⁴/16] M1; = 32 − 16 = 16 A1; second stage ½ × 2 × 8 = 8 M1; total 24 m A1

parts.label: a

parts.text: A lift in a tall building in Dubai starts from rest and moves upwards. For 0 ≤ t ≤ 2 its velocity is v = t − 0.25t² m s⁻¹. Find the velocity and the acceleration of the lift when t = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance travelled by the lift in the first 2 seconds.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The lift then moves at constant speed 1 m s⁻¹ and finally slows down to rest, the final stage taking 2 seconds and covering 4/3 m. The lift rises 30 m in total. Find the total time of the journey.
parts.working: Constant-speed distance = 30 − 8/3 = 82/3 m M1; time at constant speed = 82/3 s A1; total = 4 + 82/3 = 94/3 s A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cyclist P passes a point O at time t = 0 and continues along a straight road at a constant speed of 9 m s⁻¹. Two seconds later a motorcyclist Q starts from rest at O and follows P along the same road. The velocity of Q is (t − 2)² m s⁻¹ for t ≥ 2, where t is the time in seconds after P passed O. Writing τ = t − 2, show that Q catches up with P when τ³ − 27τ − 54 = 0.
parts.working: Displacement of Q = ∫(t − 2)² dt = (t − 2)³/3 = τ³/3 M1 A1; P: 9t = 9(τ + 2); τ³/3 = 9τ + 18 ⇒ τ³ − 27τ − 54 = 0 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the time at which Q catches up with P, the distance from O at that moment, and the speed of Q at that moment.
parts.answer: t = 8 s; 72 m from O; Q's speed 36 m s⁻¹
parts.working: (τ − 6)(τ + 3)² = 0 M1; τ = 6, so t = 8 s A1; distance = 9 × 8 = 72 m A1; v_Q = 6² = 36 m s⁻¹ A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle starts from rest at O and moves in a straight line. Its velocity, in m s⁻¹, at time t s is v = 6t − 1.5t² for 0 ≤ t ≤ 4 and v = −0.5(t − 4)(10 − t) for 4 ≤ t ≤ 10. Find the greatest speed of the particle during the 10 seconds.
parts.working: First stage: 6 − 3t = 0, t = 2, v = 6 M1 A1; second stage: minimum at t = 7, v = −4.5, speed 4.5 M1; greatest speed 6 m s⁻¹ A1

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total distance travelled by the particle and its final distance from O.
parts.answer: Total distance 34 m; finally 2 m from O (on the opposite side of O)
parts.working: ∫₀⁴ = [3t² − 0.5t³] = 16 M1 A1; ∫₄¹⁰ −0.5(t − 4)(10 − t) dt = −18 M1 A1; distance 16 + 18 = 34 m, displacement −2, so 2 m from O A1

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line. Its velocity at time t s is v = pt² + qt + r m s⁻¹, where p, q and r are constants. Initially its velocity is 5 m s⁻¹ and its acceleration is −6 m s⁻². It is at instantaneous rest when t = 1. Find p, q and r.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the distance between the two positions where the particle is at instantaneous rest.
parts.working: (t − 1)(t − 5) = 0, second rest at t = 5 B1; s = t³/3 − 3t² + 5t M1; s(1) = 7/3, s(5) = −25/3 A1; distance 32/3 m A1

parts.answer: Trapezium: (0, 0) to (8, 12), horizontal to (28, 12), down to (34, 0)

parts.text: A girl walks from her home to a shop and back. Her displacement–time graph consists of straight line segments joining the points (0, 0), (10, 50), (25, 50) and (40, 0), where time is in seconds and displacement from home is in metres. Find her velocity in each of the three stages.
parts.answer: 5 m s⁻¹, 0 m s⁻¹, −10/3 m s⁻¹

parts.label: b

parts.answer: Average speed 2.5 m s⁻¹; average velocity 0

Both cars travel along the same straight road. Sketch on the same axes the velocity-time graphs for the two cars.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A particle moves in a straight line, starting at O. Find the time at which the particle is instantaneously at rest for the first time, and the total distance travelled in the 15 seconds.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time at which the particle passes back through O, and its final displacement from O.

parts.working: Distance fallen by P = 5t², height of Q = 18t − 5t² M1; 5t² + 18t − 5t² = 45 M1; t = 2.5 A1; height = 45 − 5(2.5)² = 13.75 m A1
