parts.text: Find the exact positive value of x at which y becomes infinite for the first time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of fish, N, in a pond at time t months is modelled by dN/dt = 0.0005N(800 − N). When t = 0, N = 100. Using partial fractions, solve the differential equation to show that N = 800/(1 + 7e^(−0.4t)).
parts.working: M1 separate. M1 1/(N(800 − N)) = (1/800)(1/N + 1/(800 − N)). A1 (1/800)(ln N − ln(800 − N)) = 0.0005t + c. M1 use t = 0, N = 100. A1 ln(N/(800 − N)) = 0.4t + ln(1/7). A1 rearranged to the given form.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of fish after 5 months.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the number of fish to reach 600, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures, and state what happens to N in the long term.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy y dy/dx = x e^(2x), with y = 1 when x = 0 and y > 0. Find y² in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y dy = ∫xe^(2x) dx. M1 integration by parts. A1 ½xe^(2x) − ¼e^(2x). A1 ½y² = ½xe^(2x) − ¼e^(2x) + c, c = ¾. A1 y² = xe^(2x) − ½e^(2x) + 3/2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = y ln x, for x > 0, given that y = 1 when x = 1. Give your answer in the form y = f(x).
parts.answer: y = e^(x ln x − x + 1) = xˣe^(1 − x)
parts.working: M1 ∫(1/y) dy = ∫ln x dx. M1 by parts: ∫ln x dx = x ln x − x. A1 ln y = x ln x − x + c. A1 c = 1. A1 y = e^(x ln x − x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that y = 27e⁻² when x = 3, and evaluate this correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = (y + 2) cos 2x, and y = 1 when x = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(y + 2) dy = ∫cos 2x dx. A1 ln(y + 2). A1 ½ sin 2x + c. M1 c = ln 3. A1 y = 3e^(½ sin 2x) − 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of y, correct to 3 significant figures, and the least positive value of x at which it occurs.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy x dy/dx = y² − 1, for x > 0, y > 1, and y = 3 when x = 1. Show that y = (2 + x²)/(2 − x²).
parts.answer: ½ ln((y − 1)/(y + 1)) = ln x + ½ ln ½, so (y − 1)/(y + 1) = ½x², giving y = (2 + x²)/(2 − x²)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(y² − 1) dy = ∫1/x dx. M1 partial fractions ½(1/(y − 1) − 1/(y + 1)). A1 ½ ln(y − 1) − ½ ln(y + 1). A1 = ln x + c. M1 c = ½ ln(1/2). M1 remove logs: (y − 1)/(y + 1) = ½x². A1 rearrange to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 1.2, correct to 3 significant figures, and explain why the solution is valid only for x < √2.
parts.answer: y = 6.14; at x = √2 the denominator is zero (y → ∞)

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = cos² y tan x, for 0 ≤ x < ½π, and y = 0 when x = 0, show that tan y = ln(sec x).
parts.answer: ∫sec² y dy = ∫tan x dx gives tan y = ln(sec x) + c with c = 0
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫sec² y dy = ∫tan x dx. A1 tan y. A1 −ln(cos x) or ln(sec x). M1 use y = 0, x = 0 to find c = 0. A1 given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = π/3, giving your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy x(x + 1) dy/dx = 2y + 1, for x > 0, and y = 1.5 when x = 1. Show that 2y + 1 = 16x²/(x + 1)².
parts.answer: ½ ln(2y + 1) = ln x − ln(x + 1) + ln 4, so 2y + 1 = 16x²/(x + 1)²
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(2y + 1) dy = ∫1/(x(x + 1)) dx. B1 1/(x(x + 1)) = 1/x − 1/(x + 1). A1 ½ ln(2y + 1). A1 ln x − ln(x + 1). M1 use x = 1, y = 1.5: ½ ln 4 = ln ½ + c. A1 c = ln 4. A1 given result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y in terms of x and state the limiting value of y as x becomes very large.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Water drains from a tank so that the depth h metres after t minutes satisfies dh/dt = −k√h, where k is a constant. Initially h = 4, and after 10 minutes h = 1. Show that 2√h = 4 − 0.2t.
parts.answer: 2√h = −kt + 4; using h = 1 at t = 10 gives k = 0.2, so 2√h = 4 − 0.2t
parts.working: M1 ∫h^(−½) dh = −∫k dt. A1 2√h = −kt + c. A1 c = 4. M1 substitute t = 10, h = 1. A1 k = 0.2 and given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the depth after 5 minutes and the time at which the tank becomes empty.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a chemical reaction in a laboratory in Karachi, the mass x grams of product formed after t seconds satisfies dx/dt = 0.02(50 − x), and x = 0 when t = 0. Solve the differential equation to show that x = 50(1 − e^(−0.02t)).
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(50 − x) dx = ∫0.02 dt. A1 −ln(50 − x) = 0.02t + c. M1 c = −ln 50. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for 40 grams of product to form, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Air is pumped into a weather balloon so that its volume V cm³ at time t seconds satisfies dV/dt = 300/√V. When t = 0, V = 100. Find an expression for V^(3/2) in terms of t.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the volume when t = 10, correct to 3 significant figures, and the time at which the volume reaches 400 cm³.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = x(y + 1)²e^(−x), and y = 0 when x = 0. Show that 1/(y + 1) = (x + 1)e^(−x).
parts.working: M1 ∫(y + 1)⁻² dy = ∫xe^(−x) dx. A1 −1/(y + 1). M1 integration by parts. A1 −xe^(−x) − e^(−x). M1 use initial condition: c = 0. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 2, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables θ and y satisfy dy/dθ = y sin² θ, and y = 2 when θ = 0. Solve the differential equation, obtaining y in terms of θ.
parts.working: M1 ∫(1/y) dy = ∫sin² θ dθ. M1 use sin² θ = ½(1 − cos 2θ). A1 ½θ − ¼ sin 2θ. A1 ln y = ½θ − ¼ sin 2θ + c. M1 c = ln 2. A1 answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when θ = π, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Solve the differential equation (x + 1) dy/dx = 2y, for x > −1 and y > 0, given that y = 5 when x = 0. Give y in terms of x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of x for which y = 45.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The population P of goats on a farm in Balochistan at time t years is modelled by dP/dt = 0.1P − 20, and P = 300 when t = 0. Show that P = 200 + 100e^(0.1t).
parts.working: M1 ∫1/(0.1P − 20) dP = ∫dt. A1 10 ln(0.1P − 20) = t + c. M1 use t = 0, P = 300. A1 c = 10 ln 10. A1 rearrange to given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the time taken for the population to double, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State what would happen to the population if instead P = 200 when t = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A news item spreads through a town. The number of people, x thousand, who have heard it t days after it was posted satisfies dx/dt = kx(5 − x), where k is a constant. When t = 0, x = 1 and when t = 1, x = 2. Show that ln(4x/(5 − x)) = 5kt and find the value of k correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 separate and use partial fractions 1/(x(5 − x)) = (1/5)(1/x + 1/(5 − x)). A1 (1/5)(ln x − ln(5 − x)). A1 = kt + c. M1 t = 0, x = 1: c = (1/5) ln ¼. A1 given form. M1 t = 1, x = 2: ln(8/3) = 5k. A1 k = 0.196.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the number of people who have heard the item after 3 days, to the nearest hundred.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (x + 1) dy/dx = y² + 4, for x > −1, and y = 2 when x = 0, show that y = 2 tan(2 ln(x + 1) + ¼π).
parts.answer: ½ tan⁻¹(y/2) = ln(x + 1) + π/8, so y = 2 tan(2 ln(x + 1) + π/4)
parts.working: M1 separate: ∫1/(y² + 4) dy = ∫1/(x + 1) dx. A1 ½ tan⁻¹(y/2). A1 ln(x + 1). M1 use y = 2, x = 0. A1 c = π/8. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.2, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After its engine is switched off, a boat on Keenjhar Lake slows so that its speed v m s⁻¹ after t seconds satisfies dv/dt = −0.02v². When t = 0, v = 10. Show that v = 50/(t + 5).
parts.working: M1 ∫v⁻² dv = −∫0.02 dt. A1 −1/v = −0.02t + c. M1 c = −0.1. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed after 15 seconds and the time taken for the speed to fall to 4 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy dy/dx = e^(x + y), and y = 0 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫e^(−y) dy = ∫eˣ dx. A1 −e^(−y) = eˣ + c. M1 c = −2. A1 e^(−y) = 2 − eˣ. A1 y = −ln(2 − eˣ).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find y when x = 0.5, correct to 3 significant figures, and state the exact value that x approaches as y tends to infinity.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that dy/dx = 4 − y², with |y| < 2, and y = 0 when x = 0, show that y = 2(e^(4x) − 1)/(e^(4x) + 1).
parts.answer: (1/4) ln((2 + y)/(2 − y)) = x, so (2 + y)/(2 − y) = e^(4x), giving the result
parts.working: M1 separate. M1 partial fractions 1/(4 − y²) = (1/4)(1/(2 − y) + 1/(2 + y)). A1 (1/4)(ln(2 + y) − ln(2 − y)). A1 = x + c. B1 c = 0. M1 remove logarithms. A1 rearrange to the given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = 0.25, correct to 3 significant figures, and state the limiting value of y as x → ∞.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The variables x and y satisfy cos² x dy/dx = √y, for 0 ≤ x < ½π, with y = 1 when x = 0. Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 ∫y^(−½) dy = ∫sec² x dx. A1 2√y = tan x + c. M1 c = 2. A1 y = ¼(tan x + 2)².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of y when x = π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of users P of a ride-hailing app in a city increases at a rate proportional to P. At a certain time, when P = 2000, P is increasing at 100 users per day. Write down a differential equation relating P and t (days) and find the constant of proportionality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Taking t = 0 when P = 2000, solve the differential equation and find P when t = 10, to the nearest whole number.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A container is filled with water. When the depth of water is h cm, the volume is V = 4h³ cm³. Water leaks out through a small hole at a rate of 2√h cm³ per second. Show that dh/dt = −1/(6h^(3/2)).
parts.working: B1 dV/dh = 12h². M1 chain rule dV/dt = (dV/dh)(dh/dt) with dV/dt = −2√h. A1 given answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Initially the depth is 16 cm. Solve the differential equation and find the time taken for the container to empty, giving your answer in minutes correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A metal casting at a foundry in Gujranwala cools so that the rate of decrease of its temperature θ °C is proportional to the difference between θ and the surrounding temperature of 30 °C. Initially θ = 200 and the temperature is falling at 8.5 °C per minute. Form a differential equation and find the constant of proportionality.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Solve the differential equation and find the temperature after 20 minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time taken for the temperature to fall to 50 °C.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Gas escapes from a spherical balloon so that the rate of decrease of its volume is proportional to its radius r cm. Show that r dr/dt = −c, where c is a positive constant. [The volume of a sphere is (4/3)πr³.]
parts.working: B1 dV/dr = 4πr². M1 4πr² dr/dt = −kr. A1 r dr/dt = −c with c = k/(4π).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Initially r = 10, and after 6 seconds r = 8. Solve the differential equation to show that r² = 100 − 6t.
parts.working: M1 ∫r dr = −∫c dt. A1 ½r² = −ct + 50. A1 c = 3 and given answer.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the time at which the balloon has completely deflated, according to this model, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.4 kg is projected with speed 8 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Use an energy method to find the distance the particle travels up the plane before coming to instantaneous rest.
parts.working: M1 KE lost = PE gained: ½ × 0.4 × 8² = 0.4 × 10 × d sin 30°. A1 12.8 = 2d. A1 d = 6.4 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the particle when it has travelled 4 m up the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A child of mass 30 kg slides from rest down a playground slide in a park in Islamabad. The slide is 5 m long and its top is 2.5 m vertically above its bottom. The child reaches the bottom with speed 5 m s⁻¹. Find the work done against resistance.
parts.working: B1 PE lost = 30 × 10 × 2.5 = 750 J. B1 KE gained = ½ × 30 × 25 = 375 J. B1 WD against resistance = 375 J.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Assuming the resistance is constant, find its magnitude.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A block of mass 5 kg is pulled from rest across a rough horizontal floor by a horizontal force of 40 N. The frictional force is 25 N. Find the work done by the 40 N force and the work done against friction when the block has moved 6 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use the work-energy principle to find the speed of the block at this point.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1200 kg travels 400 m down a straight hill inclined at an angle α, where sin α = 0.05, with its engine switched off. The resistance to motion is a constant 300 N. The speed of the car at the top is 10 m s⁻¹. Find the loss in potential energy and the work done against resistance.
parts.answer: PE loss 240 000 J; WD against resistance 120 000 J

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the speed of the car at the bottom of the hill.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 2 kg is released from rest on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is 0.3. Find the work done against friction as the particle slides 12 m down the plane.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Use an energy method to find the speed of the particle after it has slid 12 m.
parts.working: M1 ½ × 2v² = 2 × 10 × 12 sin 25° − WD. A1 correct values. A1 v = 6.01.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A cyclist and her bicycle have a total mass of 75 kg. She reaches the bottom of a hill, inclined at an angle α to the horizontal where sin α = 0.06, with speed 8 m s⁻¹ and then free-wheels (does not pedal) up the hill. The resistance to motion is a constant 15 N. Find how far up the hill she travels before coming to rest.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crate of mass 25 kg is pulled along a rough horizontal floor in a warehouse by a rope inclined at 20° above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is 80 N and the coefficient of friction is 0.25. Find the normal reaction and the frictional force.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The crate passes a point A with speed 1 m s⁻¹. Use the work-energy principle to find its speed after it has moved a further 15 m.
parts.working: M1 WD by tension = 80 cos 20° × 15; WD against friction = F × 15. M1 ½ × 25(v² − 1) = difference. A1 v = 4.94.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A small block of mass 0.5 kg slides down a smooth curved ramp. It passes the point A with speed 2 m s⁻¹ and reaches the lowest point B, which is 3 m vertically below A. Find the speed of the block at B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: From B the block moves along a rough horizontal surface, where the coefficient of friction is 0.25, and comes to rest at C. Find the distance BC and the work done against friction between B and C.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The block is now replaced at A and projected with speed u m s⁻¹ so that it stops at a point 20 m beyond B. Find u.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A block of mass 3 kg is projected with speed 12 m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 30°. The coefficient of friction is 0.2. Using the work-energy principle, find the distance the block travels up the plane before coming to rest.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the block then slides back down, and find its speed when it returns to the point of projection.
parts.answer: tan 30° = 0.577 > 0.2 so it slides back; speed 8.36 m s⁻¹
parts.working: B1 component of weight 15 N > maximum friction 6 cos 30° = 5.20 N. M1 ½ × 3v² = (15 − 5.196)d. A1 correct substitution. A1 v = 8.36.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A crane on a building site in Lahore raises a load of mass 800 kg vertically from rest through a height of 20 m. At the top the load is moving at 2 m s⁻¹. Ignoring resistances, find the work done by the tension in the cable.
parts.working: B1 PE gain 160 000 J. B1 KE gain 1600 J. B1 total 161 600 J.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The lifting took 40 s. Find the average power of the crane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A ball of mass 0.2 kg is thrown vertically downwards with speed 6 m s⁻¹ from the top of a cliff 25 m above the sea at Gwadar. Ignoring air resistance, use an energy method to find the speed with which the ball hits the sea.

parts.label: b
parts.text: In fact the ball does 40 J of work against air resistance. Find the speed with which it hits the sea.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1500 kg moves up a straight hill inclined at an angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 0.1. The engine exerts a constant driving force of 2500 N and the resistance to motion is a constant 1500 N. The car passes point A at 25 m s⁻¹ and later passes point B at 15 m s⁻¹. Use the work-energy principle to find the distance AB.
parts.working: M1 work-energy equation with four terms. A1 ½ × 1500(625 − 225) = 1500 × 10 × 0.1d + 1500d − 2500d. A1 300 000 = 500d. A1 d = 600 m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the work done by the driving force between A and B and the increase in potential energy.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A skier of mass 70 kg skis down a straight slope of length 200 m at a resort in Malam Jabba. The bottom of the slope is 40 m vertically below the top. The skier's speed increases from 3 m s⁻¹ at the top to 20 m s⁻¹ at the bottom. Find the work done against resistances.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the average resistance to motion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². Particle A of mass 3 kg lies on a rough horizontal table, where the coefficient of friction is 0.2. It is attached to a light inextensible string which passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to particle B of mass 2 kg, which hangs freely. The system is released from rest. Use an energy method to find the speed of the particles when B has fallen 1.5 m (A has not reached the pulley).
parts.working: B1 PE lost by B = 2 × 10 × 1.5 = 30 J. B1 WD against friction = 0.2 × 30 × 1.5 = 9 J. M1 ½ × (3 + 2)v² = 30 − 9. A1 v² = 8.4. A1 v = 2.90.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At this instant the string breaks. Find how much further A travels along the table.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A particle of mass 0.5 kg moves up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at 20° to the horizontal. It passes point A with speed 9 m s⁻¹ and point B, 5 m further up the plane, with speed 4 m s⁻¹. Find the work done against friction between A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car travels along a straight level motorway at a constant speed of 25 m s⁻¹. The engine is working at 30 kW. Find the resistance to motion.
parts.working: M1 driving force = 30 000 ÷ 25. A1 constant speed so resistance = 1200 N.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The resistance is unchanged. Find the power needed to travel at a constant 20 m s⁻¹ on the same road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1000 kg moves along a straight level road with its engine working at 20 kW. The resistance to motion is 500 N. Find the acceleration of the car at the instant when its speed is 10 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest possible steady speed of the car on this road with the same power and resistance.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1400 kg travels at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹ up a straight hill inclined at angle α, where sin α = 0.08. The resistance to motion is 700 N. Find the power of the car's engine.

parts.label: b
parts.text: At the top of the hill the road becomes level. The power and resistance are unchanged. Find the initial acceleration of the car on the level road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1500 kg moves on a level road. The resistance to motion is kv newtons, where v m s⁻¹ is the speed and k is a constant. With the engine working at 45 kW, the greatest steady speed is 30 m s⁻¹. Find k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the car when it is travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ with the engine working at 45 kW.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A lorry of mass 8000 kg has a maximum power of 120 kW. The resistance to motion is 3000 N. Find the greatest steady speed of the lorry up a hill inclined at angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 1/40.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the lorry at an instant when it is moving up the hill at 15 m s⁻¹ with the engine at full power.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 1200 kg tows a trailer of mass 400 kg along a straight level road using a light rigid tow-bar. The resistances to motion are 400 N on the car and 200 N on the trailer. The car's engine works at 24 kW. Find the acceleration when the speed is 15 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the tension in the tow-bar at this instant.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the greatest steady speed of the car and trailer on this road with the same power.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1000 kg has a constant power P W and experiences a constant resistance R N. Its greatest steady speed up a hill inclined at angle α, where sin α = 0.05, is 20 m s⁻¹, and its greatest steady speed down the same hill is 30 m s⁻¹. Find P and R.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest steady speed of the car on a level road.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A cyclist and her bicycle have total mass 80 kg. On a level road her maximum power is 240 W and the resistance to motion is a constant 20 N. Find her greatest steady speed.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find her acceleration when she is working at 240 W and travelling at 5 m s⁻¹.
parts.working: B1 driving force 48 N. M1 48 − 20 = 80a. A1 0.35.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A train of mass 200 tonnes travels on a straight level track. Its engine has a maximum power of 800 kW and its greatest steady speed is 40 m s⁻¹. Find the resistance to motion, assumed constant.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the acceleration of the train when it is travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ at full power.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car of mass 900 kg moves on a level road with its engine working at a constant 30 kW. The resistance to motion is (400 + 2v²) N when the speed is v m s⁻¹. Find the acceleration when v = 25 and state whether the car is speeding up or slowing down.
parts.working: B1 driving force 1200 N. M1 1200 − (400 + 1250) = 900a. A1 a = −0.5, slowing down.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the greatest steady speed V satisfies V³ + 200V − 15 000 = 0 and find V correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 30 000/V = 400 + 2V². A1 V³ + 200V − 15 000 = 0. B1 V = 22.0 (by calculator / iteration).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A car of mass 1250 kg moves down a straight hill inclined at angle α, where sin α = 0.04. Its engine works at 15 kW and the resistance to motion is 900 N. Find the acceleration of the car when its speed is 20 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest steady speed of the car down the hill with the same power and resistance.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Take g = 10 m s⁻². A minibus of mass 1100 kg travels at a constant speed of 18 m s⁻¹ up a straight road which rises 1 m for every 25 m travelled along the road. The resistance to motion is 450 N. Find the power of the engine.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the work done by the engine while the minibus travels 500 m along the road.

parts.label: a

parts.working: B1 disc centre (2, 3), radius 3; B1 |z| ≥ |z − 4| ⇔ Re z ≥ 2, so R is the right-hand half of the disc.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of |z| for points in R. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 farthest point lies on the line through O and the centre (it has Re z = 2 + 6/√13 > 2, so it is in R); A1 √13 + 3 = 6.61.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the least value of Re z for points in R.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The locus L₁ is given by arg(z − 1 − i) = ¼π and the locus L₂ by |z − 5 − i| = 3. Describe each locus.
parts.answer: L₁: half-line from the point 1 + i (excluded) at angle π/4 to the positive real direction. L₂: circle centre 5 + i, radius 3.
parts.working: B1 half-line from (1, 1) at 45°; B1 circle.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find, in exact form, the complex numbers represented by the points where L₁ meets L₂.
parts.working: M1 points on L₁: (1 + t) + (1 + t)i, t > 0; M1 (t − 4)² + t² = 9 ⇒ 2t² − 8t + 7 = 0; A1 t = 2 ± √2/2 (both positive, so both points lie on the half-line); A1 both complex numbers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z satisfies |z + 2 − i| = 1. Show that the locus of z touches the real axis, and state the point of contact.
parts.answer: Centre −2 + i is 1 unit from the real axis, equal to the radius; contact at z = −2.
parts.working: B1 centre (−2, 1), radius 1; B1 distance to real axis = 1, contact at (−2, 0).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the least and greatest values of arg z for points on the locus, where −π < arg z ≤ π. Give the least value in radians correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.answer: Least ≈ 2.21 rad (exactly π − 2 tan⁻¹(½)); greatest = π
parts.working: B1 greatest is π, at the point of contact −2; M1 arg(−2 + i) = π − tan⁻¹(½) = 2.678; M1 subtract sin⁻¹(1/√5) = 0.4636 for the other tangent; A1 2.214 ≈ 2.21.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The complex number z = x + iy satisfies |z − 4i| = |z − 6|. Find the Cartesian equation of the locus of z.

parts.label: b

parts.working: M1 perpendicular distance from O to 3x − 2y − 5 = 0 is 5/√(9 + 4); A1 1.39.

parts.label: a

parts.working: M1 tan(π/3) = y/(x + 2); A1 with x > −2.

parts.label: b

parts.working: M1 z + 2 = 3 + 3√3 i; A1 argument is π/3, so yes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region R consists of points z satisfying |z − 3i| ≤ 2 and Re z ≥ 1. Find the least value of arg z for points in R. Give your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures, and show that the point where it occurs is in R.
parts.answer: ≈ 0.841 rad (π/2 − sin⁻¹(2/3)); at the tangent point Re z = 2√5/3 ≈ 1.49 ≥ 1
parts.working: M1 tangent from O to circle centre 3i, radius 2; M1 angle = π/2 − sin⁻¹(2/3); A1 0.841; B1 tangent length √(9 − 4) = √5, so Re z = √5 cos(π/2 − sin⁻¹(2/3)) = √5 × 2/3 = 2√5/3 ≈ 1.49 ≥ 1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the greatest value of |z| for points in R. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 on the circle x² + (y − 3)² = 4 we have |z|² = 6y − 5, so maximise y subject to x ≥ 1; M1 x = 1 gives y = 3 + √3; A1 |z| = √(13 + 6√3) = 4.84.

parts.label: b
parts.text: With this value of x, find the standard deviation of the prize money for one game, correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A rice mill in Sindh fills bags with a nominal mass of 5 kg. The masses are normally distributed with standard deviation 0.08 kg. An inspector suspects that the mean mass is less than 5 kg. A random sample of 20 bags has mean mass 4.962 kg. Test at the 5% significance level whether the inspector's suspicion is justified.
parts.answer: z = −2.12 < −1.645, so reject H₀: there is evidence that the mean mass is less than 5 kg.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 5, H₁: μ < 5; M1 standardise with 0.08/√20; A1 z = −2.12 (or p = 0.0168); M1 compare with −1.645 (or 0.0168 < 0.05); A1 reject H₀, conclusion in context, not over-assertive.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The lifetimes, x hours, of a random sample of 50 batteries of a certain brand were recorded, giving Σx = 1218 and Σx² = 29 900. Calculate unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The manufacturer claims that the mean lifetime is 25 hours. Test at the 2% significance level whether the mean lifetime differs from 25 hours.
parts.answer: z = −2.09; |z| < 2.326, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that the mean lifetime differs from 25 hours.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 25, H₁: μ ≠ 25; M1 standardise using √(4.684/50); A1 z = −2.09; M1 compare with ±2.326 (two-tailed 2%); A1 do not reject H₀, conclusion in context.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why it was not necessary to assume that the lifetimes are normally distributed.
parts.answer: The sample is large, so by the Central Limit Theorem the sample mean is approximately normally distributed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A food delivery company says its delivery times have mean 30 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes. After a change of routes, a random sample of 36 deliveries has mean 32.1 minutes. Assuming the standard deviation is unchanged, test at the 1% significance level whether the mean delivery time has increased.
parts.answer: z = 2.1 < 2.326, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence at 1% that the mean has increased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 30, H₁: μ > 30; M1 (32.1 − 30)/(6/√36); A1 z = 2.1; M1 compare with 2.326; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the p-value of the test and state the smallest significance level, to the nearest 0.1%, at which H₀ would be rejected.
parts.working: M1 1 − Φ(2.1); A1 0.0179, so reject at levels above 1.79%.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The scores in an aptitude test are normally distributed with mean 60 and standard deviation 4.5. A coaching centre suspects that students from a certain region score lower on average. A random sample of 25 such students is taken. Find the critical region for the sample mean for a test at the 5% significance level.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 60, H₁: μ < 60; M1 60 − 1.645 × 4.5/√25; A1 58.52; B1 critical region stated as x̄ < 58.52.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The sample mean is found to be 58.7. State, with a reason, the conclusion of the test.
parts.answer: 58.7 is not in the critical region, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that students from the region score lower.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The heights of seedlings of a certain plant after 4 weeks are normally distributed with mean 12.4 cm and standard deviation 1.8 cm. A gardener uses a new fertiliser on 40 randomly chosen seedlings and their mean height after 4 weeks is 12.95 cm. Assuming the standard deviation is unchanged, test at the 5% significance level whether the fertiliser increases the mean height.
parts.answer: z = 1.93 > 1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean height has increased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 12.4, H₁: μ > 12.4; M1 (12.95 − 12.4)/(1.8/√40); A1 1.93; M1 compare with 1.645; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A machine fills bottles with mineral water. The volume is normally distributed with mean 500 ml and standard deviation 4 ml when the machine is working correctly. A random sample of 15 bottles has mean volume 498.1 ml. Test at the 10% significance level whether the mean volume has changed.
parts.answer: z = −1.84; |z| > 1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean volume has changed.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ ≠ 500; M1 (498.1 − 500)/(4/√15); A1 −1.84; M1 compare with ±1.645 (5% in each tail); A1 reject H₀, in context.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one assumption about the sample needed for the test to be valid.
parts.answer: The sample is random (the bottles are chosen independently).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The masses of mangoes from an orchard are normally distributed with mean 80 g and standard deviation 10 g. After a new irrigation system is installed, a random sample of n mangoes has mean mass 82.5 g. A test at the 5% significance level of H₀: μ = 80 against H₁: μ > 80 leads to rejection of H₀. Find the least possible value of n.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A test of H₀: μ = 15 against H₁: μ ≠ 15 is carried out on a normal population with standard deviation 2.4. A random sample of size 30 gives a sample mean of 15.82. Find the p-value of the test.

parts.label: b

parts.label: a
parts.text: The journey time, x minutes, of a bus route in Karachi was recorded for a random sample of 60 journeys, giving Σ(x − 40) = 90 and Σ(x − 40)² = 1505. Find unbiased estimates of the population mean and variance of the journey time.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The bus company states that the mean journey time is 40 minutes. Test at the 1% significance level whether the mean journey time is greater than 40 minutes.
parts.answer: z = 2.41 > 2.326, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean journey time is greater than 40 minutes.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 40, H₁: μ > 40; M1 1.5/√(23.22/60); A1 2.41; M1 compare with 2.326; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A health magazine claims that university students sleep 8 hours per night on average. A researcher believes the true mean is lower. The number of hours of sleep is normally distributed with standard deviation 1.2 hours. A random sample of 50 students has mean 7.6 hours. Explain why a one-tailed test is appropriate.
parts.answer: The researcher is only looking for evidence that the mean is lower than 8.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Carry out the test at the 5% significance level.
parts.answer: z = −2.36 < −1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the mean sleep time is less than 8 hours.
parts.working: B1 H₀: μ = 8, H₁: μ < 8; M1 (7.6 − 8)/(1.2/√50); A1 −2.36; M1 compare with −1.645; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A factory tests whether the mean breaking strength of its cables has fallen below 400 N, using a 5% significance level. Explain what is meant by a Type I error in this context.
parts.answer: Concluding that the mean breaking strength has fallen below 400 N when in fact it has not.
parts.working: B1 rejecting H₀ when it is true, in context.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a Type II error in this context.
parts.answer: Concluding that the mean breaking strength has not fallen when in fact it has fallen below 400 N.
parts.working: B1 not rejecting H₀ when it is false, in context.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the probability of making a Type I error.
parts.working: B1 equal to the significance level (the test statistic has a continuous distribution).

parts.label: a
parts.text: In the past, 30% of customers at a bakery bought a cake. After the price rises, the owner tests H₀: p = 0.3 against H₁: p < 0.3 using a random sample of 20 customers. He will reject H₀ if 2 or fewer customers buy a cake. Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that the true proportion is now 0.15, find the probability of a Type II error.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The number of complaints received by a call centre per day has a Poisson distribution. In the past the mean was 4. A manager will conclude that the mean has increased if 9 or more complaints are received on a randomly chosen day. Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.text: The masses of bags of sugar filled by a machine are normally distributed with standard deviation 6 g. A test of H₀: μ = 1000 against H₁: μ < 1000 uses a random sample of 36 bags and rejects H₀ if the sample mean is less than 998.355 g. Show that the significance level of the test is 5%.

parts.label: c

parts.answer: It would decrease, because the true mean is further below the critical value, so the sample mean is more likely to fall in the critical region.

parts.text: Sara suspects that a coin is biased towards heads. She tosses it 10 times and will conclude that it is biased if she obtains 8 or more heads. Find the probability of a Type I error.

parts.label: b

parts.answer: Type II, because she did not reject H₀ (H₀ could be false).

parts.text: The number of breakdowns of a fleet of buses has a Poisson distribution with mean 2.5 per week. parts.label: b

parts.answer: P(X ≥ 10) = 0.0197 < 0.025, so reject H₀: evidence that the probability of a six is not 1/6.

parts.answer: 8 is not in the critical region, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that the proportion has changed.

parts.label: b

parts.answer: Do not reject H₀ (7 is not in the critical region); the result is only just not significant, so a larger trial would be sensible.
parts.working: B1 conclusion in context; B1 sensible comment.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calls to a helpline arrive at random at a mean rate of 3.2 per 10 minutes. After a television advert, 7 calls arrive in a randomly chosen 10-minute period. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean rate has increased.
parts.answer: P(X ≥ 7) = 0.0446 < 0.05, so reject H₀: evidence that the rate has increased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: λ = 3.2, H₁: λ > 3.2; M1 Po(3.2); M1 1 − P(X ≤ 6); A1 0.0446; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A typist makes errors at random at a mean rate of 1.8 per page. After using new software, a random sample of 5 pages contains 4 errors in total. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean rate has decreased.
parts.answer: P(X ≤ 4) = 0.0550 > 0.05, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that the error rate has decreased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: λ = 9 (for 5 pages), H₁: λ < 9; M1 Po(9); M1 P(X ≤ 4); A1 0.0550; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Accidents on a stretch of motorway occur at random at a mean rate of 0.6 per week. Speed cameras are installed, and in the following 12 weeks there are 2 accidents. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean rate has decreased.
parts.answer: P(X ≤ 2) = 0.0255 < 0.05, so reject H₀: evidence that the accident rate has decreased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: λ = 7.2 (for 12 weeks), H₁: λ < 7.2; M1 Po(7.2); M1 P(X ≤ 2); A1 0.0255; A1 conclusion in context.

parts.label: b

parts.answer: Accidents occur independently of each other (and at a constant average rate).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Emails arrive at an office inbox at random at a mean rate of 4 per hour. After a new website is launched, 52 emails arrive in a randomly chosen 10-hour period. Use a suitable approximating distribution to test at the 5% significance level whether the mean rate has increased.
parts.answer: N(40, 40) with continuity correction: z = (51.5 − 40)/√40 = 1.82 > 1.645, so reject H₀: evidence that the rate has increased.
parts.working: B1 H₀: λ = 40, H₁: λ > 40; B1 approximate by N(40, 40) (λ > 15); M1 continuity correction 51.5; M1 standardise; A1 z = 1.82 (p = 0.0345); A1 compare with 1.645 and conclude in context.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c

parts.answer: 10 is not in the critical region, so do not reject H₀: insufficient evidence that the mean has changed.

parts.working: M1 first application: −eˣ cos x + ∫eˣ cos x dx; M1 second: eˣ sin x − ∫eˣ sin x dx; A1 I = ½eˣ(sin x − cos x); M1 limits: ½e^π(0 + 1) − ½(0 − 1); A1 ½(e^π + 1); A1 ≈ 12.07.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ x² e^{−x} dx.
parts.working: M1 u = x², v = −e^{−x}; A1 −x²e^{−x} + ∫2x e^{−x} dx; M1 second application; A1 −e^{−x}(x² + 2x + 2) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x² e^{−x} dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₁^e (ln x)² dx = e − 2.
parts.working: M1 u = (ln x)², v = x; A1 x(ln x)² − ∫2 ln x dx; M1 ∫ln x dx = x ln x − x by parts; A1 x(ln x)² − 2x ln x + 2x; M1 limits (e − 2e + 2e) − (0 − 0 + 2); A1 e − 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that x cos²x ≡ ½x + ½x cos 2x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/2} x cos²x dx.
parts.working: B1 ∫½x dx = ¼x²; M1 parts on ½x cos 2x: ¼x sin 2x − ¼∫sin 2x dx; A1 ¼x sin 2x + ⅛ cos 2x; M1 limits: π²/16 + (−⅛ − ⅛); A1 π²/16 − ¼.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 1 + x³ to find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x²(1 + x³)⁴ dx.
parts.working: M1 du = 3x² dx; A1 ⅓∫u⁴ du with limits 1 and 2; M1 (1/15)[u⁵]₁²; A1 31/15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = sin x to find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/2} cos x/(1 + sin x)² dx.
parts.working: M1 du = cos x dx, limits 0 and 1; A1 ∫₀¹(1 + u)⁻² du; M1 [−(1 + u)⁻¹]₀¹; A1 −½ + 1 = ½.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = √x to find the exact value of ∫₁⁴ e^{√x}/√x dx.
parts.working: M1 dx = 2u du, limits 1 and 2; A1 ∫₁² 2eᵘ du; M1 2[eᵘ]₁²; A1 2e² − 2e.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = x − 2 to find the exact value of ∫₂³ x(x − 2)⁵ dx.
parts.working: M1 x = u + 2, limits 0 and 1; A1 ∫₀¹(u⁶ + 2u⁵) du; M1 [u⁷/7 + u⁶/3]₀¹; A1 10/21.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution x = tan θ to show that ∫₀¹ 1/(1 + x²)² dx = ∫₀^{π/4} cos²θ dθ.
parts.working: M1 dx = sec²θ dθ; A1 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ so integrand becomes sec²θ/sec⁴θ = cos²θ; A1 limits 0 and π/4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀¹ 1/(1 + x²)² dx.
parts.working: M1 cos²θ = ½(1 + cos 2θ); M1 ½[θ + ½ sin 2θ]; A1 π/8 + ¼.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 1 + ln x to find the exact value of ∫₁^e √(1 + ln x)/x dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = eˣ + 1 to show that ∫₀^{ln 3} e^{2x}/(eˣ + 1) dx = 2 − ln 2.
parts.working: M1 du = eˣ dx and eˣ = u − 1; A1 integral becomes ∫(u − 1)/u du; B1 limits 2 and 4; M1 [u − ln u]₂⁴; A1 2 − ln 4 + ln 2 = 2 − ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: By writing sin³x = (1 − cos²x) sin x and using the substitution u = cos x, find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/3} sin³x dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution x = 3 sin θ to find the exact value of ∫₀^{3/2} √(9 − x²) dx.
parts.working: M1 dx = 3 cos θ dθ, √(9 − 9 sin²θ) = 3 cos θ; A1 ∫9 cos²θ dθ; B1 limits 0 and π/6; M1 (9/2)[θ + ½ sin 2θ]; A1 (9/2)(π/6 + √3/4); A1 3π/4 + 9√3/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = √(x + 1) to find the exact value of ∫₀³ x/(1 + √(x + 1)) dx.
parts.working: M1 x = u² − 1, dx = 2u du; B1 limits 1 and 2; M1 (u² − 1)/(1 + u) = u − 1; A1 ∫₁² 2u(u − 1) du; M1 2[u³/3 − u²/2]₁²; A1 5/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = tan x to find the exact value of ∫₀^{π/4} tan²x sec⁴x dx.
parts.working: M1 du = sec²x dx; M1 sec²x = 1 + u²; A1 ∫₀¹ u²(1 + u²) du; M1 [u³/3 + u⁵/5]; A1 8/15.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the substitution u = 2 + cos x to show that ∫₀^{π/2} sin 2x/(2 + cos x) dx = 2 − 4 ln(3/2).
parts.working: M1 sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x; M1 du = −sin x dx, cos x = u − 2; A1 ∫₂³ 2(u − 2)/u du (limits reversed with sign); M1 2[u − 2 ln u]₂³; A1 2(1 − 2 ln 3 + 2 ln 2); A1 2 − 4 ln(3/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 6 − x² meets the line y = 2 at the points P and Q. Find the x-coordinates of P and Q.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curve and the line.
parts.working: M1 ∫(4 − x²) dx; M1 [4x − x³/3] from −2 to 2; A1 32/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the points where the line y = 10 − x meets the curve y = x² − 2x + 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the line and the curve.
parts.working: M1 ∫(6 + x − x²) dx; M1 limits −2 and 3; A1 125/6.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x³ and the line y = 4x meet at the origin and at the point A in the first quadrant. Find the coordinates of A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region in the first quadrant enclosed between the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curve y = √x and the line y = ½x.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the curves y = 4/x² and y = 5 − x² meet where x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0, and hence find the x-coordinates of their points of intersection for x > 0.
parts.working: M1 4 = 5x² − x⁴; A1 equation; A1 (x² − 1)(x² − 4) = 0 → x = 1, 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the two curves for x > 0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curves y = x² − 2x and y = 6x − x².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve y = x² + 1 at the point (2, 5).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the curve, the tangent and the y-axis.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region bounded by the curves y = eˣ and y = e^{−x} and the line x = ln 3.
parts.working: B1 the curves meet at x = 0; M1 ∫₀^{ln 3}(eˣ − e^{−x}) dx; A1 [eˣ + e^{−x}]; M1 (3 + ⅓) − (1 + 1); A1 4/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line x + y = 10 meets the curve y = 9/x at the points A and B. Find the x-coordinates of A and B.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region enclosed between the line and the curve, giving your answer in the form p − q ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = kx, where 0 < k < 4, meets the curve y = 4x − x² at the origin and at the point P. Find the x-coordinate of P in terms of k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Show that the area enclosed between the line and the curve is (4 − k)³/6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Given that this area is 9/2, find k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the x-coordinates of the first two points where the curves y = sin x and y = cos x meet for x > 0.
parts.working: M1 tan x = 1; A1 both values.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact area of the region enclosed between the two curves between these points.
parts.working: M1 ∫(sin x − cos x) dx (sin x above); A1 [−cos x − sin x]; M1 limits: (√2/2 + √2/2) − (−√2/2 − √2/2); A1 2√2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 2x^{3/2} and the line y = 8x meet at the origin and at the point A. Find the coordinates of A.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the area of the region enclosed between the curve and the line.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 3/(2x + 5) dx, for x > −5/2.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(ax + b) dx = (1/a) ln(ax + b) with a = 2; A1 (3/2) ln(2x + 5) + c (ln|2x + 5| accepted).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀² 3/(2x + 5) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: (3/2) ln 9 − (3/2) ln 5; A1 (3/2) ln(9/5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (6x − 1)/(3x² − x + 2) dx.
parts.working: B1 6x − 1 is the derivative of 3x² − x + 2; M1 ∫ f′(x)/f(x) dx = ln f(x) + c; A1 ln(3x² − x + 2) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ (6x − 1)/(3x² − x + 2) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 [ln(3x² − x + 2)]₀¹ = ln 4 − ln 2; A1 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁^e (2 + 1/x) dx, giving your answer in an exact form.
parts.working: B1 integral 2x + ln x; M1 limits (2e + ln e) − (2 + ln 1); A1 2e − 1 (ln e = 1, ln 1 = 0).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 5/(1 − 2x) dx, for x < ½.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(b − ax) dx = −(1/a) ln(b − ax) with a = 2, b = 1; A1 −(5/2) ln(1 − 2x) + c (check: differentiating gives 5/(1 − 2x)).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (x² + 3x + 4)/(x + 1) can be written as x + 2 + 2/(x + 1).
parts.working: M1 divide, or write x² + 3x + 4 = (x + 1)(x + 2) + 2; A1 result shown with remainder 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀³ (x² + 3x + 4)/(x + 1) dx, giving your answer in the form p + q ln 2, where p and q are rational.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has gradient dy/dx = (2x + 3)/(x² + 3x) for x > 0, and passes through the point (1, 0). Find y in terms of x.
parts.answer: y = ln(x² + 3x) − ln 4, i.e. y = ln((x² + 3x)/4)
parts.working: M1 the numerator is the derivative of the denominator, so y = ln(x² + 3x) + c; M1 substitute (1, 0): ln 4 + c = 0; A1 c = −ln 4; A1 y = ln((x² + 3x)/4).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the x-coordinate of the point on this curve where y = ln 2, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 ln((x² + 3x)/4) = ln 2 gives x² + 3x = 8; M1 solve x² + 3x − 8 = 0 and take the positive root (−3 + √41)/2; A1 x = 1.70.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ eˣ/(1 + eˣ) dx.
parts.working: B1 the numerator eˣ is the derivative of the denominator 1 + eˣ; A1 ln(1 + eˣ) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀^{ln 3} eˣ/(1 + eˣ) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: ln(1 + e^{ln 3}) − ln(1 + e⁰) = ln 4 − ln 2; A1 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₁^k 2/(x + 1) dx = ln 8, where k > 1, find the exact value of k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (x³ + 2x)/(x⁴ + 4x² + 3) dx, for all real x.
parts.working: B1 the denominator f = x⁴ + 4x² + 3 has f′ = 4x³ + 8x = 4(x³ + 2x); M1 ∫ f′/(4f) dx = ¼ ln f; A1 ¼ ln(x⁴ + 4x² + 3) + c (f > 0 for all x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ (x³ + 2x)/(x⁴ + 4x² + 3) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 ¼[ln(x⁴ + 4x² + 3)]₀¹ = ¼(ln 8 − ln 3); A1 ¼ ln(8/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ dx/(x ln x) for x > 1.
parts.working: B1 the denominator x ln x is the product of ln x and its derivative 1/x, so the integrand is f′(x)/f(x) with f(x) = ln x; M1 ∫ f′/f dx = ln f + c; A1 ln(ln x) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫_e^{e²} dx/(x ln x), giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 [ln(ln x)] from e to e² = ln 2 − ln 1; A1 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (2x³ + 3x² + 1)/(x² + x) = 2x + 1 + 1/x − 2/(x + 1) for x > 0.
parts.answer: 2x³ + 3x² + 1 = (x² + x)(2x + 1) + (1 − x), and (1 − x)/(x(x + 1)) = 1/x − 2/(x + 1), so the result is shown.
parts.working: M1 long division gives quotient 2x + 1 and remainder 1 − x; M1 partial fractions of (1 − x)/(x(x + 1)) with coefficient 1 (x = 0) and −2 (x = −1); A1 full result shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₁³ (2x³ + 3x² + 1)/(x² + x) dx, giving your answer in the form p + ln(q/r), where p, q and r are integers.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₀^k (2x − 6)/(x² − 6x + 10) dx = ln(k² − 6k + 10) − ln 10 for k > 0.
parts.answer: The numerator 2x − 6 is the derivative of x² − 6x + 10, which is positive for all x, so the integral is [ln(x² − 6x + 10)]₀^k = ln(k² − 6k + 10) − ln 10 (shown).
parts.working: M1 numerator is the derivative of the denominator; A1 limits give the result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the two values of k for which ∫₀^k (2x − 6)/(x² − 6x + 10) dx = ln ½.
parts.working: M1 ln(k² − 6k + 10) − ln 10 = ln ½, so k² − 6k + 10 = 5; M1 k² − 6k + 5 = 0, so (k − 1)(k − 5) = 0; A1 k = 1 or k = 5 (both positive).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ dx/(x(2 + ln x)) for x > e⁻².
parts.working: B1 the denominator f(x) = 2 + ln x has f′(x) = 1/x, so the integrand is f′/f; M1 ∫ f′/f dx = ln f + c; A1 ln(2 + ln x) + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₁^e dx/(x(2 + ln x)), giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 [ln(2 + ln x)] from 1 to e = ln 3 − ln 2; A1 ln(3/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (2e^{3x} − e^{−x}) dx.
parts.working: M1 ∫ e^{ax} dx = (1/a)e^{ax} used with a = 3 and a = −1; A1 (2/3)e^{3x} + e^{−x} + c.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀^{ln 2} e^{2x} dx, giving your answer as an exact number.
parts.working: B1 integral ½e^{2x}; M1 ½(e^{2 ln 2} − e⁰) = ½(4 − 1); A1 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k e^{x/2} dx = 6, find the exact value of k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ e^{−2x} dx.
parts.working: B1 antiderivative −½e^{−2x}; M1 (−½e⁻²) − (−½); A1 ½(1 − e⁻²).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has gradient dy/dx = 4e^{2x} − 3 and passes through (0, 5). Find y in terms of x.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 2e^{2x} − 3x + c; M1 use (0, 5): 2 + c = 5; A1 c = 3, so y = 2e^{2x} − 3x + 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the value of y when x = ln 2, giving your answer in the form p − q ln 2, with p and q integers.
parts.working: M1 substitute x = ln 2: 2e^{2 ln 2} − 3 ln 2 + 3 = 8 − 3 ln 2 + 3; A1 11 − 3 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀^{ln 2} (eˣ + e^{−x})² dx, giving your answer in the form p + q ln 2, where p and q are rational.
parts.working: M1 expand: e^{2x} + 2 + e^{−2x}; M1 integrate: ½e^{2x} + 2x − ½e^{−2x}; A1 value at ln 2 is 2 + 2 ln 2 − 1/8; A1 value at 0 is 0, so the answer is 15/8 + 2 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₀¹ (eˣ − e^{−x}) dx = (e − 1)²/e.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative eˣ + e^{−x}; M1 (e + e⁻¹) − (1 + 1); A1 e − 2 + 1/e, and (e − 1)²/e = (e² − 2e + 1)/e = e − 2 + 1/e.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the value of a for which ∫₀^a 3e^{−3x} dx = 0.95, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that e^{2x}/(eˣ + 1) = eˣ − eˣ/(eˣ + 1).
parts.answer: eˣ(eˣ + 1) − eˣ = e^{2x}, so the identity is shown.
parts.working: M1 put the right side over the common denominator eˣ + 1: (eˣ(eˣ + 1) − eˣ)/(eˣ + 1); A1 numerator is e^{2x}, shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find the exact value of ∫₀^{ln 4} e^{2x}/(eˣ + 1) dx.
parts.working: B1 ∫eˣ dx = eˣ; M1 ∫ eˣ/(eˣ + 1) dx = ln(eˣ + 1), since the numerator is the derivative of the denominator; M1 [eˣ − ln(eˣ + 1)] from 0 to ln 4 = (4 − ln 5) − (1 − ln 2); A1 3 − ln(5/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x e^{x²} dx.
parts.working: B1 x e^{x²} is ½ times the derivative of e^{x²}; M1 ½[e^{x²}] from 0 to 1; A1 ½(e − 1).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function f satisfies f″(x) = 6e^{2x} − 4e^{−x}, with f′(0) = 1. Find f′(x).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given also that f(0) = 2, find f(x).

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the exact value of f(ln 2).
parts.working: M1 substitute x = ln 2, using e^{2 ln 2} = 4 and e^{−ln 2} = ½: 6 − 2 − 6 ln 2 + 9/2; A1 17/2 − 6 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀^{ln 3} eˣ/(1 + e^{2x}) dx.
parts.working: M1 substitute u = eˣ (du = eˣ dx, limits 1 to 3): ∫₁³ du/(1 + u²); A1 [arctan u] from 1 to 3; M1 arctan 3 − arctan 1; A1 arctan 3 − π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (eˣ − 1)² eˣ = e^{3x} − 2e^{2x} + eˣ.
parts.working: M1 expand the square and multiply by eˣ; A1 result shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀^{ln 2} (eˣ − 1)² eˣ dx exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁³ (4x − 1/x²) dx, giving your answer as an exact fraction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² (x² − 2x − 3) dx.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁² 6(3x − 2)² dx.
parts.working: M1 integrate using the chain rule: (2/3)(3x − 2)³; M1 limits (2/3)(4³) − (2/3)(1³); A1 42.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₁^a (2x + 1) dx = 12, where a > 1, find a correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 integral = [x² + x] from 1 to a = a² + a − 2; M1 a² + a − 2 = 12, so a² + a − 14 = 0; A1 a = (−1 + √57)/2 = 3.27.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k (6x² − 4x) dx = 14, where k > 0, find k correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 integral = [2x³ − 2x²] from 0 to k = 2k³ − 2k²; M1 2k³ − 2k² = 14, so k³ − k² − 7 = 0; M1 sign change of 2k³ − 2k² − 14 between 2.305 and 2.315 (or iteration); A1 k = 2.31.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀¹ x(1 − x)⁴ dx.
parts.working: M1 expand: x − 4x² + 6x³ − 4x⁴ + x⁵ (or substitute u = 1 − x); M1 integrate term by term; A1 ½ − 4/3 + 3/2 − 4/5 + 1/6; A1 1/30.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₁⁴ (√x + 4/x²) dx, giving your answer as an exact fraction.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that (x + 1)²/x² = 1 + 2/x + 1/x².
parts.working: B1 expand the numerator and divide each term by x².

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₁² (x + 1)²/x² dx = 3/2 + 2 ln 2.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative x + 2 ln x − 1/x; M1 limits (2 + 2 ln 2 − ½) − (1 + 0 − 1); A1 3/2 + 2 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫_a^{a+2} (4x − 3) dx = 20, find the value of a.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative 2x² − 3x; M1 limits: 2(a + 2)² − 3(a + 2) − (2a² − 3a) = 8a + 2; M1 8a + 2 = 20; A1 a = 9/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A function f(x) = ax² + bx, where a and b are constants, satisfies ∫₀² f(x) dx = 10 and ∫₀¹ f(x) dx = 2. Find a and b.
parts.working: M1 ∫₀² f = 8a/3 + 2b = 10; M1 ∫₀¹ f = a/3 + b/2 = 2; M1 eliminate b (b = 4 − 2a/3) to get 4a/3 + 8 = 10; A1 a = 3/2; A1 b = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₁² (x − 2/x)² dx = 1/3.
parts.working: M1 expand: x² − 4 + 4/x²; M1 integrate: x³/3 − 4x − 4/x; A1 limits (8/3 − 8 − 2) − (1/3 − 4 − 4); A1 = 1/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₁^p (3x² − 2px) dx = 9, where p > 1, find p.
parts.working: M1 antiderivative x³ − px²; M1 limits (p³ − p·p²) − (1 − p) = p − 1; M1 p − 1 = 9; A1 p = 10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² |x² − 1| dx.
parts.working: B1 x² − 1 ≤ 0 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1 and ≥ 0 for 1 ≤ x ≤ 2, so split the integral at x = 1; M1 ∫₀¹ (1 − x²) dx = 2/3; M1 ∫₁² (x² − 1) dx = (8/3 − 2) − (1/3 − 1) = 4/3; A1 total 2/3 + 4/3 = 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = 2x + 1, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid, then give it correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀² (2x + 1)² dx; M1 integrate: π[(2x + 1)³/6] from 0 to 2; A1 π(125 − 1)/6 = 62π/3 ≈ 64.9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = √x, for 1 ≤ x ≤ 4, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₁⁴ y² dx = π∫₁⁴ x dx; M1 π[x²/2] from 1 to 4; A1 π(8 − ½) = 15π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The line y = 3x, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis, forming a solid. Find its exact volume.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀² (3x)² dx = 9π∫₀² x² dx; M1 9π[x³/3] from 0 to 2 = 24π; A1 24π (a cone of radius 6 and height 2: ⅓π·6²·2 = 24π).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = √(4 − x²), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀² (4 − x²) dx; M1 π[4x − x³/3] from 0 to 2; A1 π(8 − 8/3) = 16π/3 (half of a sphere of radius 2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by y = eˣ, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 1 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume, and give it to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀¹ (eˣ)² dx = π∫₀¹ e^{2x} dx; M1 π[½e^{2x}] from 0 to 1; A1 π(e² − 1)/2; A1 ≈ 10.0.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = 4 − x² and the x-axis is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 the curve meets the x-axis at x = ±2, so V = π∫₋₂² (4 − x²)² dx; M1 = 2π∫₀² (16 − 8x² + x⁴) dx by symmetry; M1 2π[16x − 8x³/3 + x⁵/5] from 0 to 2; A1 2π(256/15) = 512π/15 ≈ 107.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by y = 1/(x + 1), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2 is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the line y = kx, the x-axis, and the line x = 3, where k > 0, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. The volume of the solid is 36π. Find k.
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀³ k²x² dx = πk²[x³/3] from 0 to 3 = 9πk²; M1 9πk² = 36π; A1 k² = 4; A1 k = 2 (k > 0).

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curves y = √x and y = x², for 0 ≤ x ≤ 1, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 washer method: V = π∫₀¹ ((√x)² − (x²)²) dx; M1 the curves meet at x = 0 and x = 1, and √x is the upper curve on this interval; M1 integrand x − x⁴; A1 π[x²/2 − x⁵/5] from 0 to 1; A1 π(½ − ⅕) = 3π/10.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the curve y = x², the y-axis, and the line y = 4, with x ≥ 0, is rotated through 360° about the y-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 for this region x = √y, so x² = y and V = π∫₀⁴ x² dy; M1 = π∫₀⁴ y dy = π[y²/2] from 0 to 4; A1 π(8) = 8π.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express sin²x in terms of cos 2x.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The region between the curve y = sin x, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = π is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Hence show that the volume of the solid is π²/2.
parts.answer: V = π∫₀^π sin²x dx = π²/2 (≈ 4.93), shown
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₀^π sin²x dx; M1 = (π/2)∫₀^π (1 − cos 2x) dx; A1 (π/2)[x − ½ sin 2x] from 0 to π = (π/2)π; A1 V = π²/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region between the curve y = 4 − x² (above) and the line y = 2 − x (below), for −1 ≤ x ≤ 2, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid.
parts.working: M1 meeting points: 4 − x² = 2 − x gives x² − x − 2 = 0, so x = −1 and x = 2; M1 V = π∫₋₁² [(4 − x²)² − (2 − x)²] dx; M1 integrand 12 + 4x − 9x² + x⁴; A1 [12x + 2x² − 3x³ + x⁵/5] from −1 to 2 = 21.6; A1 V = 108π/5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by y = 1/√x, the x-axis, and the lines x = 1 and x = k, where k > 1, is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Show that the volume is π ln k.
parts.answer: V = π∫₁^k (1/x) dx = π[ln x] from 1 to k = π ln k (shown).
parts.working: M1 V = π∫₁^k (x^{−1/2})² dx = π∫₁^k x⁻¹ dx; M1 π[ln x] from 1 to k = π(ln k − 0); A1 V = π ln k.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact value of k for which the volume is 2π.
parts.working: M1 π ln k = 2π, so ln k = 2; A1 k = e².

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region bounded by the line y = 2x + 3, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 4.
parts.working: M1 the line is above the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, so area = ∫₀⁴ (2x + 3) dx; M1 [x² + 3x] from 0 to 4 = 16 + 12; A1 28.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = 6/(x + 2) is drawn for x ≥ 1. Find the exact area bounded by the curve, the x-axis, and the lines x = 1 and x = 4.
parts.working: M1 ∫₁⁴ 6/(x + 2) dx = [6 ln(x + 2)] from 1 to 4; M1 6(ln 6 − ln 3); A1 6 ln 2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area of the region between the curve y = 4 − x², the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: M1 the curve is above the x-axis for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2; M1 ∫₀² (4 − x²) dx = [4x − x³/3] from 0 to 2; A1 8 − 8/3 = 16/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x² − 5x + 4 crosses the x-axis at x = 1 and x = 4. Find the area of the region between the curve and the x-axis for 1 ≤ x ≤ 4.
parts.working: B1 for 1 < x < 4 the curve is below the x-axis, so area = −∫₁⁴ y dx; M1 ∫₁⁴ (x² − 5x + 4) dx = [x³/3 − 5x²/2 + 4x] from 1 to 4; A1 the integral is −9/2; A1 area = 9/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The region bounded by the curve y = 2e^{−x/2}, the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 4 has area A. Find A in the form p(1 − e⁻²), where p is an integer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the area bounded by the curve y = 1/√(3x + 1), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 5.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that the curve y = x³ − 4x can be written as y = x(x − 2)(x + 2), and state the x-coordinates where it meets the x-axis for −2 ≤ x ≤ 2.
parts.answer: y = x(x − 2)(x + 2); the curve meets the x-axis at x = −2, 0 and 2.
parts.working: B1 x³ − 4x = x(x² − 4) = x(x − 2)(x + 2); B1 the roots are −2, 0 and 2.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area of the regions between the curve and the x-axis for −2 ≤ x ≤ 2.
parts.working: B1 for −2 ≤ x ≤ 0 the curve is above the axis: ∫₋₂⁰ (x³ − 4x) dx = 0 − (4 − 8) = 4; M1 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 the curve is below the axis: ∫₀² (x³ − 4x) dx = 4 − 8 = −4, so that area is 4; M1 add the two areas; A1 total 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The area under the curve y = k/(x + 1) from x = 0 to x = 3 is ln 8. Find the value of k.
parts.working: M1 area = k[ln(x + 1)] from 0 to 3 = k ln 4; M1 k ln 4 = ln 8; A1 k = ln 8/ln 4; A1 k = 3/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The curve y = x(x − 2)² is drawn for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 (it touches the x-axis at x = 2). Find the area between the curve and the x-axis.
parts.working: M1 y ≥ 0 on [0, 2], so area = ∫₀² x(x − 2)² dx; M1 = ∫₀² (x³ − 4x² + 4x) dx; A1 [x⁴/4 − 4x³/3 + 2x²] from 0 to 2 = 4 − 32/3 + 8; A1 4/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area bounded by the curve y = 2x/(x + 1)², the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that y = x³ − 3x² = x²(x − 3), and state the sign of y for −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.
parts.answer: y = x²(x − 3). For −1 ≤ x < 3 with x ≠ 0, x² > 0 and x − 3 < 0, so y < 0; y = 0 only at x = 0 (touching) and at x = 3.
parts.working: B1 factorise x³ − 3x² = x²(x − 3); B1 x² ≥ 0 and x − 3 < 0 on the interval, so y ≤ 0.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the total area between the curve and the x-axis for −1 ≤ x ≤ 3.
parts.working: B1 y ≤ 0 on the whole interval, so area = −∫₋₁³ y dx; M1 ∫(x³ − 3x²) dx = [x⁴/4 − x³]; M1 value at 3 is −27/4 and at −1 is 5/4, so the integral is −27/4 − 5/4 = −8; A1 area = 8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area bounded by the curve y = 3x²/(x³ + 4), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: B1 the numerator 3x² is the derivative of x³ + 4, which is positive; M1 ∫₀² = [ln(x³ + 4)] from 0 to 2; A1 ln 12 − ln 4; A1 ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact area bounded by the curve y = 1/(x² + 4), the x-axis, and the lines x = 0 and x = 2.
parts.working: M1 ∫ dx/(x² + a²) = (1/a) arctan(x/a) with a = 2; M1 ½[arctan(x/2)] from 0 to 2; A1 ½(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 3/((x + 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ 3/((x + 1)(x + 2)) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln(x + 1) − 3 ln(x + 2); M1 limits (3 ln 2 − 3 ln 3) − (0 − 3 ln 2); A1 6 ln 2 − 3 ln 3 = 3 ln(4/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (5x + 1)/(x² − 1) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₂³ (5x + 1)/(x² − 1) dx, giving your answer in the form p ln 2 − q ln 3, with p and q integers.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln(x − 1) + 2 ln(x + 1); M1 limits (3 ln 2 + 2 ln 4) − (3 ln 1 + 2 ln 3); A1 7 ln 2 − 2 ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.working: M1 combine the right side over (x − 2)(x + 2); A1 numerator (x + 2) − (x − 2) = 4, so the result is shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₃⁵ 1/(x² − 4) dx = ¼ ln(15/7).
parts.working: M1 integrate: ¼[ln(x − 2) − ln(x + 2)]; M1 limits ¼[(ln 3 − ln 7) − (ln 1 − ln 5)]; A1 ¼ ln(15/7).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x + 3)/(x(x + 1)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₁² (2x + 3)/(x(x + 1)) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln x − ln(x + 1); M1 limits (3 ln 2 − ln 3) − (0 − ln 2); A1 4 ln 2 − ln 3 = ln(16/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x² + 4)/(x² − x − 2) in the form A + B/(x − 2) + C/(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₃⁴ (x² + 4)/(x² − x − 2) dx, giving your answer in the form 1 + p ln 2 − q ln 5, where p and q are rational.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that (5x + k)/((x + 1)(x − 3)) ≡ A/(x + 1) + 2/(x − 3) for all x other than −1 and 3, find the values of the constants k and A.
parts.working: M1 multiply through: 5x + k = A(x − 3) + 2(x + 1); M1 x = 3 gives 15 + k = 8, so k = −7; M1 x = −1 gives −5 + k = −4A, so A = 3; A1 k = −7 and A = 3.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ (5x − 7)/((x + 1)(x − 3)) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: 3 ln(x + 1) + 2 ln|x − 3|; M1 limits: at 1, 2 ln 2 and at 0, 2 ln 3 (|x − 3| = 2 and 3); A1 3 ln 2 + 2 ln 2 − 2 ln 3 = ln(32/9).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (x + 4)/(x²(x − 2)) in the form A/x + B/x² + C/(x − 2).
parts.working: M1 B: multiply by x² and set x = 0: B = 4/(0 − 2) = −2; M1 C: set x = 2 in (x + 4)/x²: C = 6/4 = 3/2; M1 compare coefficients (large x gives A + C = 0), so A = −3/2; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₃⁴ (x + 4)/(x²(x − 2)) dx = (3/2) ln(3/2) − 1/6.
parts.working: M1 integrate: −(3/2) ln x + 2/x + (3/2) ln(x − 2); M1 use limits 3 and 4; A1 (3/2)(ln 3 − ln 2) + (½ − ⅔) = (3/2) ln(3/2) − 1/6.

parts.label: a
parts.working: M1 combine the right side over (x + 1)(x + 3); A1 numerator 2(x + 3) − 2(x + 1) = 4, so the identity is shown.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^k 4/((x + 1)(x + 3)) dx = ln 4, find the value of k.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express x/((x + 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₀¹ x/((x + 1)(x + 2)) dx = ln(9/8).
parts.working: M1 integrate: −ln(x + 1) + 2 ln(x + 2); M1 limits (−ln 2 + 2 ln 3) − (0 + 2 ln 2); A1 2 ln 3 − 3 ln 2 = ln(9/8).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 1/((x − 1)²(x + 1)) in the form A/(x − 1) + B/(x − 1)² + C/(x + 1).
parts.working: M1 B = 1/(x + 1) at x = 1 gives B = ½; M1 C = 1/(x − 1)² at x = −1 gives C = ¼; M1 x = 0 gives −A + B + C = 1, so A = −¼; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence find ∫₂³ 1/((x − 1)²(x + 1)) dx, giving your answer exactly in the form p + q ln(2/3).
parts.working: M1 integrate: −¼ ln(x − 1) − ½(x − 1)⁻¹ + ¼ ln(x + 1); M1 value at 3 is ¼ ln 2 − ¼ and at 2 is −½ + ¼ ln 3; A1 difference ¼ + ¼ ln(2/3).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 1/(x(x² + 1)) in the form A/x + Bx/(x² + 1).
parts.working: M1 A = 1 (multiply by x and set x = 0); M1 A(x² + 1) + Bx² = 1 gives A + B = 0, so B = −1; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence show that ∫₁^{√3} 1/(x(x² + 1)) dx = ½ ln(3/2).
parts.working: M1 integrate: ln x − ½ ln(x² + 1); M1 limits: (½ ln 3 − ½ ln 4) − (0 − ½ ln 2); A1 ½ ln 3 − ln 2 + ½ ln 2; A1 ½ ln(3/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express 1/(4 − x²) in partial fractions.
parts.working: M1 set up A/(2 − x) + B/(2 + x) with A(2 + x) + B(2 − x) = 1; M1 x = 2 gives A = ¼ and x = −2 gives B = ¼; A1 result.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀¹ dx/(4 − x²), giving your answer in the form ¼ ln k.
parts.working: M1 integrate: ¼[ln(2 + x) − ln(2 − x)] from 0 to 1 = ¼ ln 3 − 0; A1 ¼ ln 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Express (2x² + 3x − 1)/(x³ − x) in partial fractions, given that x³ − x = x(x − 1)(x + 1).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₂³ (2x² + 3x − 1)/(x³ − x) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: M1 integrate: ln x + 2 ln(x − 1) − ln(x + 1); M1 limits (ln 3 + 2 ln 2 − ln 4) − (ln 2 + 0 − ln 3); A1 2 ln 3 − ln 2; A1 ln(9/2).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ 1/(x² + 9) dx.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(x² + a²) dx = (1/a) arctan(x/a) with a = 3; A1 (1/3) arctan(x/3) + c.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² 4/(x² + 4) dx, giving your answer in exact form.
parts.working: B1 ∫ 4/(x² + 4) dx = 4 × ½ arctan(x/2) = 2 arctan(x/2); M1 2(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 π/2.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² 2x/(x² + 5) dx, giving your answer as an exact logarithm.
parts.working: B1 the numerator 2x is the derivative of x² + 5, so the antiderivative is ln(x² + 5); M1 ln 9 − ln 5; A1 ln(9/5).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₋₁¹ 1/(x² + 2x + 5) dx.
parts.working: M1 complete the square: x² + 2x + 5 = (x + 1)² + 4; M1 ∫ 1/((x + 1)² + 2²) dx = ½ arctan((x + 1)/2); M1 ½[arctan 1 − arctan 0]; A1 π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀^{½} 3/(4x² + 1) dx, giving your answer in terms of π.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 1/(4x² + 1) dx = ¼ × 2 arctan(2x) = ½ arctan(2x), so ∫ 3/(4x² + 1) dx = (3/2) arctan(2x); M1 (3/2)(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 3π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (x + 1)/(x² + 4) dx.
parts.working: B1 split: (x + 1)/(x² + 4) = x/(x² + 4) + 1/(x² + 4); M1 x/(x² + 4) gives ½ ln(x² + 4) and 1/(x² + 4) gives ½ arctan(x/2); A1 result + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀² (x + 1)/(x² + 4) dx, giving your answer in the form ½ ln 2 + π/8.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: ½ ln 8 − ½ ln 4 + ½(arctan 1 − arctan 0); A1 ½ ln 2 + π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (2x − 3)/(x² − 2x + 5) dx.
parts.working: M1 write 2x − 3 = (2x − 2) − 1; M1 the first part gives ln(x² − 2x + 5); M1 complete the square: x² − 2x + 5 = (x − 1)² + 4, so ∫ 1/((x − 1)² + 4) dx = ½ arctan((x − 1)/2); A1 result + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₁³ (2x − 3)/(x² − 2x + 5) dx, giving your answer exactly.
parts.working: M1 limits: (ln 8 − ½ arctan 1) − (ln 4 − ½ arctan 0); A1 ln 2 − π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Given that ∫₀^a 3/(x² + a²) dx = π/4, where a > 0, find the value of a.
parts.working: M1 ∫ 3/(x² + a²) dx = (3/a) arctan(x/a); M1 limits (3/a)(arctan 1) = (3/a)(π/4); M1 (3/a)(π/4) = π/4, so a = 3; A1 a = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A curve has gradient dy/dx = 6/(x² + 2x + 10) and passes through (−1, 0). Show that y = 2 arctan((x + 1)/3).
parts.working: M1 complete the square: x² + 2x + 10 = (x + 1)² + 9; M1 ∫ 6/((x + 1)² + 3²) dx = 2 arctan((x + 1)/3) + c; A1 at (−1, 0), arctan 0 = 0, so c = 0; A1 y = 2 arctan((x + 1)/3).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the exact x-coordinate of the point on the curve with x > −1 where y = π/3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀¹ x/(x⁴ + 1) dx.
parts.working: M1 substitute u = x², du = 2x dx (limits 0 to 1); M1 ½∫₀¹ du/(1 + u²) = ½[arctan u] from 0 to 1; A1 ½ × π/4; A1 π/8.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the exact value of ∫₀² 1/(2x² + 8x + 12) dx, giving your answer in the form (√2/4)(arctan p − arctan q), where p and q are exact.
parts.working: B1 2x² + 8x + 12 = 2((x + 2)² + 2); M1 ∫ du/(u² + 2) = (1/√2) arctan(u/√2) with u = x + 2; A1 the factor ½ × (1/√2) = √2/4; M1 limits arctan(4/√2) − arctan(2/√2); A1 (√2/4)(arctan(2√2) − arctan(√2)).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find ∫ (3x + 2)/(x² + 2x + 5) dx.
parts.working: M1 write 3x + 2 = (3/2)(2x + 2) − 1; M1 the first part gives (3/2) ln(x² + 2x + 5); A1 complete the square (x + 1)² + 4 and integrate −1/((x + 1)² + 4) to −½ arctan((x + 1)/2); A1 result + c.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Hence evaluate ∫₀² (3x + 2)/(x² + 2x + 5) dx, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
parts.working: M1 substitute limits: (3/2) ln(13/5) − ½(arctan(3/2) − arctan(½)); A1 1.17.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Show that ∫₀¹ x²/(x² + 1) dx = 1 − π/4.
parts.working: M1 write x²/(x² + 1) = 1 − 1/(x² + 1); M1 integrate: x − arctan x; A1 [x − arctan x] from 0 to 1; A1 1 − π/4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate ∫₀² (x + 1)/(x² + 4x + 8) dx, giving your answer in terms of logarithms, arctan 2 and π.
parts.working: B1 x + 1 = ½(2x + 4) − 1; M1 ½ ln(x² + 4x + 8) from the first part; M1 complete the square (x + 2)² + 4, giving −½ arctan((x + 2)/2); M1 limits: (½ ln 20 − ½ arctan 2) − (½ ln 8 − ½ arctan 1); A1 ½ ln(5/2) − ½ arctan 2 + π/8.

stem:
The ages, in years, of the 19 people attending a morning yoga class in Islamabad are shown in the stem-and-leaf diagram.
2 | 3 7 9
3 | 1 4 4 8
4 | 1 2 5 7 8
5 | 2 5 6 8
6 | 1 3
7 | 0
Key: 3 | 4 means 34 years

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median and the quartiles of the ages.
parts.working:
n = 19, so median is the 10th value, Q1 the 5th and Q3 the 15th.
B1 median 45
B1 Q1 = 34
B1 Q3 = 56

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the interquartile range and the range of the ages.

author: HomiLabs

stem:
A driving school in Lahore measured the reaction times, in seconds, of 15 learner drivers using a computer test.
0.2 | 1 4 8
0.3 | 0 1 3 5 6 8 9
0.4 | 2 4 7
0.5 | 1 8
Key: 0.3 | 5 means 0.35 seconds

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the median reaction time and the interquartile range.
parts.working:
B1 median = 8th value = 0.36
M1 Q1 = 4th value 0.30, Q3 = 12th value 0.44
A1 IQR 0.14 s

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the percentage of the drivers whose reaction time was more than 0.40 s.

author: HomiLabs

stem:
The numbers of samosas sold by a stall in Rawalpindi on 23 days in Ramadan were:
48  62  55  71  39  58  66  52  47  80  61  54  45  59  63  57  68  50  43  74  56  104  60

parts.label: a
parts.text: Draw a stem-and-leaf diagram to represent the data, using stems 3, 4, 5, …, 10 and including a key.
parts.working:
B1 correct stems including empty stem 9
B1 leaves correct and in order
B1 key

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the median and the interquartile range.
parts.working:
n = 23: median 12th value, Q1 6th, Q3 18th
B1 median 58
M1 Q1 = 50, Q3 = 66

stem: A machine fills bags of rice that are nominally 2 kg. The masses of the bags are normally distributed with standard deviation 0.05 kg. A random sample of 25 bags has mean mass 2.012 kg. Test, at the 5% significance level, H₀: μ = 2 against H₁: μ ≠ 2, where μ is the population mean mass.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why a two-tailed test is appropriate here.
parts.answer: The question is whether the mean differs from 2 kg in either direction (it could be too high or too low), so H₁: μ ≠ 2.
parts.working: B1 a difference in either direction is being tested

parts.label: b
parts.text: Carry out the test, giving the test statistic and the critical values.
parts.working:
M1 z = (x̄ − μ) ÷ (σ ÷ √n) = (2.012 − 2) ÷ (0.05 ÷ 5)
A1 z = 1.20
B1 two-tailed 5% critical values ±1.96

parts.label: c
parts.text: State your conclusion in context.
parts.answer: Since 1.2 lies between −1.96 and 1.96, H₀ is not rejected: there is no evidence at the 5% level that the mean mass of the bags differs from 2 kg.
parts.working:
B1 not significant, H₀ not rejected
B1 conclusion in context (mean mass not shown to differ from 2 kg)
